1	# Design: test attributes in Maester 3.0
2	
3	Status: accepted for implementation, 2026-10-11. This document replaces the `Category`, `Preview` and tag rules of
4	the [3.0 design](./maester-3.0-design.md) (sections 3.2, 4 and 7.1). Everything else in that design stands.
5	
6	## 1. Summary
7	
8	In 2.x and in the first 3.0 previews a test was described by one free-text `Category` and a list of free-form
9	tags. Between them they carried eight different ideas: suite, product, topic, benchmark control, benchmark
10	version, licence, severity and theme. Neither could drive a clean report filter, and a new idea meant a new tag
11	convention.
12	
13	This design gives each idea its own typed attribute, drawn from a closed list where a list makes sense, and
14	stops using tags for Maester's own taxonomy. A test answers six questions:
15	
16	| Question | Attributes |
17	| --- | --- |
18	| Which test is this? | `Id`, `Title` |
19	| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` |
20	| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` |
21	| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` |
22	| Can it run here? | `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` |
23	| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` |
24	
25	`Category` and `Preview` are removed. `Tag` stays as a free label for the owner of a test folder and no longer
26	carries taxonomy. The rules for choosing each value are in the
27	[attribute rubric](../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md); this document specifies the mechanics.
28	
29	## 2. The attribute
30	
31	```powershell
32	[MaesterTest(
33	    Id                 = 'MT.1012',
34	    Title              = 'MFA is required for risky sign-ins',
35	
36	    Product            = 'entra',
37	    Feature            = 'conditional-access',
38	    Area               = 'authentication',
39	    ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
40	
41	    Severity           = 'High',
42	    UserImpact         = 'Low',
43	    ImplementationCost = 'Low',
44	
45	    Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),
46	
47	    Service            = 'Graph',
48	    License            = 'AAD_PREMIUM_P2',
49	    Author             = 'f-bader'
50	)]
51	```
52	
53	### 2.1 Properties
54	
55	Types stay within what the AST reader accepts: `string`, `string[]` and `bool`.
56	
57	| Property | Type | Values | Built-in tests | Notes |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| `Id` | string | unchanged | required | |
60	| `Title` | string | unchanged | required | |
61	| `Product` | string | a product key or alias from the taxonomy | required | Stored and written to results as the key. Custom tests may use any one-line text up to 40 characters. |
62	| `RelatedProduct` | string[] | product keys or aliases | optional | Must not repeat `Product`. Resolved like `Product`. |
63	| `Feature` | string | a feature key of the test's product | required | Custom tests: any one-line text up to 60 characters. |
64	| `Area` | string | an area key | required | Custom tests: any one-line text up to 60 characters. |
65	| `ResourceType` | string | a resource type key | required | Pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`. Custom tests may use a key that is not in the taxonomy. |
66	| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info` | required | unchanged |
67	| `UserImpact` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | required unless `Severity` is `Info` | Normalised to this spelling. |
68	| `ImplementationCost` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | required unless `Severity` is `Info` | Normalised to this spelling. |
69	| `Mitre` | string[] | `T####`, `T####.###`, or the single value `None` | required | `None` cannot be combined with an ID. IDs are validated against the pinned ATT&CK release by the build and the unit tests, not at run time. |
70	| `Control` | string[] | `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>` | optional; required for a test of a suite that declares `Frameworks` | Pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.\-]*:[^\s,]+$`. The requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports. It is the only way a test is mapped to a framework (section 6). Any test may use it. For a framework shipped with Maester the requirement must exist in its file. |
71	| `Service` | string[] | unchanged | required | |
72	| `License` | string[] | unchanged | optional | |
73	| `Permission` | string[] | `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`; `\|` joins alternatives | optional | Replaces the reserved name `GraphScope`. See section 2.4. Recorded; not enforced in 3.0. |
74	| `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` | string[] | unchanged | optional | |
75	| `Lifecycle` | string | `Preview`, `Stable`, `Deprecated` | optional, default `Stable` | Replaces `Preview`. |
76	| `ReplacedBy` | string | a test ID | optional | Only meaningful with `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'`. |
77	| `Tag` | string[] | unchanged syntax | optional | Free labels. See section 5. |
78	| `LongRunning`, `Exclusive`, `InstanceSource`, `Author`, `Contributor`, `HelpUrl` | | unchanged | unchanged | |
79	
80	Removed properties and the error the reader gives for each:
81	
82	| Property | Message |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| `Category` | "`Category` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Product` and `Feature`; the result's `Block` is derived from them." |
85	| `Preview` | "`Preview` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Lifecycle = 'Preview'`." |
86	
87	Both are `InvalidMetadata` with that message, so a preview-era custom test fails loudly with the fix in the text.
88	`Convert-MtTest` writes the new form.
89	
90	Reserved names become `OptionalService` and `TimeoutSeconds`. `GraphScope` and `Deprecated` are no longer
91	reserved: `Permission` and `Lifecycle` took their places.
92	
93	### 2.2 The taxonomy registry
94	
95	`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` lists the products (with their features and aliases), the areas and the
96	resource types. Keys are lowercase kebab-case for products, features and areas and PascalCase for resource
97	types. Display names live only in the registry, so a product can be renamed without touching a test.
98	
99	- The reader resolves `Product` and `RelatedProduct` through `Key` and `Aliases`, case-insensitively, the same way
100	  service names resolve through the service registry. `Product = 'Entra ID'` therefore still loads and is stored as
101	  `entra`.
102	- For a built-in test, a `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` or `ResourceType` that is not in the registry, or a
103	  `Feature` that does not belong to the test's `Product`, is `InvalidMetadata`.
104	- For a custom test, a value that matches the registry is normalised to the key; any other value is kept as written.
105	- The schema table's `Products` list is removed. The order of `Products` in the registry is the order of the
106	  console lanes and of product lists in reports.
107	- `Get-MtTaxonomy` (internal) loads and caches the registry; `Get-MtTestSchema` keeps its role.
108	
109	`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json` is a trimmed copy of one MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise release:
110	tactic and technique IDs and names, and the IDs that release retired. The registry's `Attack.Version` names the
111	release. `build/attack/Update-MtAttackTechniques.ps1` regenerates the file from the official STIX data when the
112	pin moves.
113	
114	### 2.3 Derived values
115	
116	Nothing in this list is typed in a test.
117	
118	| Value | Rule |
119	| --- | --- |
120	| `Suite`, `Source` | From the nearest `suite.json`, as today. |
121	| `Block` | Kept on the result row for 2.x consumers and for XML test-case names. Native tests: the display name of `Product` when it resolves in the registry; else `Product` as written; else `Feature`; else the suite's `Name`; else `Custom`. Pester-format tests: the `Describe` or `Context` name, as today. |
122	| Tactics | Looked up from `Mitre` in the pinned ATT&CK file when a consumer needs them. |
123	| Selection tags | See section 5. |
124	
125	`Convert-MtTest` writes the `Describe` name of a converted Pester test to `Feature`, so its `Block`, and with it
126	its CI test-case name, does not change.
127	
128	### 2.4 Permission
129	
130	Added 2026-10-23, before any built-in test used the property. The first user is the Active Directory suite
131	(maester365/maester#2483); Graph scopes follow in a scripted pass.
132	
133	**Grammar.** Each element is one permission, `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`, or several joined with `|`.
134	
135	- `Service` is a service-registry key or alias, stored as the key. For a built-in test it must be one of the
136	  test's `Service` values. A custom test may name any service, for example a pack connector's.
137	- `Kind` is one of the kinds the registry lists for the service (`PermissionKinds` in
138	  `MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1`): `Scope`, `DelegatedScope`, `ApplicationScope` and `Role` for Graph; `Role` and
139	  `Action` for Azure; `Role` and `Cmdlet` for Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and Teams; `Ldap`, `Cim`,
140	  `File`, `Remoting` and `Group` for Active Directory; and so on. Each kind has an example and a description,
141	  which the docs and the test builder show.
142	- `Name` is the rest of the string after the second colon, as the product spells it. It may contain colons
143	  (GitHub's `administration:read`, a Google scope URL). The engine does not parse it; a suite may document a
144	  sub-grammar for its own kinds (Active Directory's `Ldap:[<partition>/]<objectClass>[.<attribute>]:<right>`).
145	- No commas, as for every list property. `|` is reserved as the separator; no permission vocabulary uses it.
146	
147	**Meaning.** The identity needs every element (all-of, like `Service`). Inside an element any one alternative
148	is enough, and the first is the least privileged. In logic terms the list is an AND of ORs, the form in which
149	Microsoft documents each Graph API (one need, a least privileged permission and higher privileged ones). Any
150	condition can be written this way: "(A and B) or C" is `('A | C', 'B | C')`.
151	
152	`License` is the other way round (the list is any-of and `&` is all-of) because a test usually needs one of
153	several SKUs. A test usually needs several permissions at once, and an OR of ANDs would have to list every
154	combination. The operator in the string always says what it means.
155	
156	**Why one string and not a structured value.** The reader accepts only string constants and a C# attribute
157	property cannot be a hashtable. A string with a fixed prefix also matches `Control` (`<framework-key>:<id>`).
158	
159	**Why not a protocol-first format.** The five-segment `<protocol>:<category>:<objectClass>:<attribute>:<right>`
160	form first proposed for Active Directory leaves out the service, embeds Maester's internal collector names, and
161	has no place for Graph scopes, roles, Azure RBAC or connector scopes. Its detail survives as the name of the
162	Active Directory kinds.
163	
164	**Normalisation and validation.** The reader writes a registered service and kind in their registry spelling and
165	puts one space around each `|`. It rejects a value that does not fit the grammar, a duplicate alternative and a
166	duplicate element. For a built-in test it also rejects an unregistered service, a service the test does not list
167	and a kind the registry does not list for the service.
168	
169	**What uses it.** The result row and the catalog carry the list as written. Planned, not part of this change: a
170	generated least-privilege page per service (the first alternative of every element of the selected tests), a
171	"Requires" line in the report, and a `Skipped` / `MissingPermission` reason for services where the engine can see
172	the identity's grants before a test runs (Graph token scopes and Entra roles, pack connector scopes; the packs
173	design's `MissingScope` would become this reason).
174	
175	## 3. Results and catalog
176	
177	Every native row gains these fields. Fields that a test does not declare are written as `null` or an empty
178	list, never omitted.
179	
180	`Product` (now the key), `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `UserImpact`,
181	`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`.
182	
183	`Tag` on a row holds the authored tags (plus instance tags of a family) and nothing else: no suite tags, no test
184	ID, no flags.
185	
186	The result gains one top-level object so a consumer can render names without the module:
187	
188	```json
189	"Taxonomy": {
190	  "Products":      [{ "Key": "entra", "Name": "Entra ID" }],
191	  "Features":      [{ "Product": "entra", "Key": "conditional-access", "Name": "Conditional Access" }],
192	  "Areas":         [{ "Key": "authentication", "Name": "Authentication" }],
193	  "ResourceTypes": [{ "Key": "Tenant" }],
194	  "Attack":        { "Version": "19.2", "Techniques": [{ "Id": "T1110", "Name": "Brute Force", "Tactics": ["TA0006"] }],
195	                     "Tactics": [{ "Id": "TA0006", "Name": "Credential Access" }] }
196	}
197	```
198	
199	It lists only the keys and techniques that the rows of that result use. Pester-format rows carry the new fields
200	as `null`.
201	
202	The built-in catalog (`Maester.TestCatalog.json`) receives the same properties through the existing generic copy,
203	plus the full `Taxonomy`. The build fails when a built-in test names a technique that is unknown or retired in
204	the pinned release.
205	
206	The console keeps one lane per product. It reads the lane title and order from the registry.
207	
208	## 4. Selection
209	
210	`Invoke-Maester` and the `Selection` section of the run config gain typed selectors:
211	
212	| Parameter | Config key | Matches |
213	| --- | --- | --- |
214	| `-Product` | `Selection.Product` | `Product` or any `RelatedProduct`. Aliases resolve. |
215	| `-Feature` | `Selection.Feature` | `Feature` |
216	| `-Area` | `Selection.Area` | `Area` |
217	| `-Severity` | `Selection.Severity` | The effective severity |
218	| `-Suite` | `Selection.Suite` | `Suite` |
219	
220	Each takes a list. Values within one selector are alternatives; different selectors must all match, and they
221	combine the same way with `-Tag` and `-TestId`. `*` wildcards work as they do for tags. `Get-MtTest` takes the
222	same five parameters. Excluding by attribute is not added in 3.0; `-ExcludeTag` and `-ExcludeTestId` remain.
223	
224	Default exclusions stop being tags:
225	
226	- A test with `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` is not run unless `-IncludePreview` is given, any `-Tag` is given, or its
227	  exact ID is in `-TestId`. This is the 2.x rule for the `Preview` tag.
228	- `LongRunning` keeps its rule.
229	- A test whose service is opt-in in the service registry, such as Active Directory, is not run unless that
230	  service is connected. The `AD` tag no longer decides this.
231	- `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'` tests still run. The row says so, and reports may set them apart.
232	
233	## 5. Tags
234	
235	Built-in tests ship without taxonomy tags. `Tag` remains for labels a test owner finds useful and for custom tests.
236	
237	### 5.1 Selecting with 2.x tags
238	
239	`-Tag CA`, `-Tag CIS`, `-ExcludeTag MS.AAD.3.5` and every other 2.x tag string keep working for the 3.x line.
240	
241	- `powershell/assets/Maester.LegacyTags.json` maps each 2.x tag to the IDs of the built-in tests that carried it.
242	  It is generated once from the frozen 2.x snapshot (`powershell/tests/fixtures/golden/tags-and-blocks.json`) and
243	  from the tags that 3.0 previews carried, and is not edited by hand afterwards. Tests added after 3.0 are not in it.
244	- When resolving `-Tag` and `-ExcludeTag`, a built-in test's selection tags are its authored `Tag` values, the
245	  `Tags` of its suite, its legacy tags from that file, and its own ID. Suite tags, legacy tags and the ID are used
246	  for selection only and are never written to a result row.
247	- A custom native test matches on its authored tags and its suite's tags. Its ID is selected with `-TestId`.
248	- The first time a run selects through a legacy tag, Maester writes one warning that names the tag and, where
249	  the file gives one, the typed selector that replaces it, for example `-Tag CA` → `-Feature conditional-access`.
250	- A unit test asserts that every tag in the 2.x snapshot still selects exactly the set of test IDs it selected in 2.x.
251	
252	### 5.2 What replaces each kind of tag
253	
254	| 2.x tag | Example | Now |
255	| --- | --- | --- |
256	| Suite | `CISA`, `Maester` | `-Suite cisa`; `Suite` on the row |
257	| Product or service | `EXO`, `Entra` | `-Product exchange`; `Product` on the row |
258	| Topic or theme | `CA`, `AD.User`, `Privileged` | `-Feature conditional-access`, `-Area privileged-access` |
259	| Benchmark control ID | `MS.AAD.3.5` | `-TestId CISA.MS.AAD.3.5`; `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.5'` on the test |
260	| Benchmark version, level, profile | `CIS M365 v7.0.0`, `L1`, `CIS E3 Level 1` | The suite's framework file (section 6) |
261	| Licence | `Entra ID P1` | `License` on the row |
262	| Severity | `Severity:High` | `-Severity High` |
263	| Lifecycle | `Deprecated`, `Preview` | `Lifecycle` |
264	
265	## 6. Benchmarks and framework files
266	
267	A test is mapped to a framework in one place, its `Control` attribute:
268	
269	```powershell
270	Control = 'cis-m365:5.2.2.3'
271	```
272	
273	This is the same for a CIS or CISA test, for a Maester test that supports one of their requirements, and for a
274	custom test. There is no second mechanism: a framework file does not list tests, and a test's ID prefix means
275	nothing to the engine.
276	
277	A framework file is the catalogue of a framework. A suite that holds one declares it in its `suite.json`:
278	
279	```json
280	"Frameworks": [
281	  { "Key": "cis-m365", "Version": "7.0.0" }
282	]
283	```
284	
285	The file is `frameworks/<key>.json` beside the `suite.json`:
286	
287	```json
288	{
289	  "Framework": "cis-m365",
290	  "Name": "CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark",
291	  "Version": "7.0.0",
292	  "Url": "https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365",
293	  "Requirements": [
294	    { "Id": "5.2.2.3", "Level": "L1", "Profile": ["E3 Level 1"] }
295	  ]
296	}
297	```
298	
299	It holds what a `key:id` string cannot: the name and version of the framework, the facts about each requirement
300	that used to be tags (level, profile, criticality, upstream status), the `Related` controls of other frameworks,
301	and the full list of requirements, so that a gap or a mistyped ID is found. A `Tests` key on a requirement and an
302	`IdPrefix` key in the declaration are ignored.
303	
304	- Frameworks are looked up by key across every suite: the suites shipped with Maester and the suites under the
305	  user's test folder. A key that two suites declare is a problem that names both `suite.json` files.
306	- A row's `Benchmark` is built from the first `Control` value, in the order of the attribute, that names a
307	  requirement of a valid framework file: `{ "Framework": "cis-m365", "Version": "7.0.0", "Requirement": "5.2.2.3" }`
308	  plus the requirement's own facts. It is `null` when no value does.
309	- A row's `Control` list is the test's `Control` values followed by the `Related` references of every requirement
310	  they name, each once.
311	- The catalog build fails on a problem with a declaration or a file, on a key declared twice, and on a built-in
312	  test whose `Control` names a loaded framework and a requirement its file does not have. A run only warns.
313	- Reports say a test supports a control. They do not state compliance with a framework.
314	
315	Framework files for CIS Microsoft 365, CIS GitHub and CISA SCuBA ship with their suites. The CISA file carries
316	each policy's revision, SHALL or SHOULD, and the NIST SP 800-53 mapping that ScubaGear publishes.
317	
318	## 7. Enforcement
319	
320	1. **Reader and build.** Section 2 rules. An invalid built-in test fails the build.
321	2. **Unit tests**, `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1`:
322	   - every built-in test has the required attributes of section 2.1;
323	   - every key is in the taxonomy and every feature belongs to its product;
324	   - `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` are absent when `Severity` is `Info` and present otherwise;
325	   - `Mitre` is a valid list for the pinned release, with no technique listed beside one of its own
326	     sub-techniques, and at most five entries;
327	   - no built-in test carries a tag that is a product, feature, area, suite or severity name, a benchmark label
328	     or a test ID;
329	   - a `Control` that names a framework shipped with Maester names a requirement of its file, and every test of a
330	     suite that declares `Frameworks` has a `Control` for a requirement of one of them;
331	   - the taxonomy has no unused or duplicate key, the folder of a test agrees with its `Product`, and the
332	     rubric's area table lists exactly the areas of the registry.
333	
334	   Whether `ResourceType` should be `Tenant` cannot be decided mechanically (a test that checks that one policy
335	   exists may still list the policies that satisfy it), so that rule is left to the attribute review.
336	3. **Attribute review.** A pull request that adds a test or changes a rubric attribute is checked by a reviewer
337	   model against the rubric page. The check fails when a value does not fit, and reports the expected value and
338	   the reason. The workflow runs trusted code from the base branch only and treats the pull request's files as data.
339	
340	## 8. Migration
341	
342	- One script, `build/migration/Convert-MtTestAttributes.ps1`, rewrites the attribute of every built-in test:
343	  it drops `Category`, turns `Preview` into `Lifecycle`, writes `Product` as a key, removes the 2.x tags and
344	  merges the values in `build/migration/attributes/*.json` when that folder exists. It is idempotent. EIDSCA and
345	  ORCA take their values from their generator metadata files and are regenerated, never edited. The values files
346	  were removed after the migration ran; the values now live in the tests and in the generator metadata.
347	- The golden test stops comparing `Block` and tags with the 2.x snapshot and asserts section 5.1 instead.
348	- `Get-MtTestInventory`, kept for one major version, reports `Feature` where it reported the `Describe` name.
349	
350	## 9. Compatibility
351	
352	| Consumer | Effect |
353	| --- | --- |
354	| `-Tag`, `-ExcludeTag` with 2.x tags | Unchanged for built-in tests, with a warning once per run. |
355	| Result `Block` | Changes for built-in tests to the product name. CI test-case names of built-in tests change once. |
356	| Result `Tag` | Built-in rows no longer list suite, product or benchmark tags or the test ID. Use the typed fields. |
357	| Result `Product` | Now a key. `Taxonomy.Products` gives the name. |
358	| Custom native tests written for a 3.0 preview | `Category` and `Preview` are rejected with the replacement in the message. `Convert-MtTest` and `New-MtTest` write the new form. |
359	| Pester-format tests | No change. |

# Design: test attributes in Maester 3.0

Status: accepted for implementation, 2026-10-11. This document replaces the `Category`, `Preview` and tag rules of
the [3.0 design](./maester-3.0-design.md) (sections 3.2, 4 and 7.1). Everything else in that design stands.

## 1. Summary

In 2.x and in the first 3.0 previews a test was described by one free-text `Category` and a list of free-form
tags. Between them they carried eight different ideas: suite, product, topic, benchmark control, benchmark
version, licence, severity and theme. Neither could drive a clean report filter, and a new idea meant a new tag
convention.

This design gives each idea its own typed attribute, drawn from a closed list where a list makes sense, and
stops using tags for Maester's own taxonomy. A test answers six questions:

| Question | Attributes |
| --- | --- |
| Which test is this? | `Id`, `Title` |
| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` |
| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` |
| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` |
| Can it run here? | `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` |
| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` |

`Category` and `Preview` are removed. `Tag` stays as a free label for the owner of a test folder and no longer
carries taxonomy. The rules for choosing each value are in the
[attribute rubric](../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md); this document specifies the mechanics.

## 2. The attribute

```powershell
[MaesterTest(
    Id                 = 'MT.1012',
    Title              = 'MFA is required for risky sign-ins',

    Product            = 'entra',
    Feature            = 'conditional-access',
    Area               = 'authentication',
    ResourceType       = 'Tenant',

    Severity           = 'High',
    UserImpact         = 'Low',
    ImplementationCost = 'Low',

    Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),

    Service            = 'Graph',
    License            = 'AAD_PREMIUM_P2',
    Author             = 'f-bader'
)]
```

### 2.1 Properties

Types stay within what the AST reader accepts: `string`, `string[]` and `bool`.

| Property | Type | Values | Built-in tests | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | string | unchanged | required | |
| `Title` | string | unchanged | required | |
| `Product` | string | a product key or alias from the taxonomy | required | Stored and written to results as the key. Custom tests may use any one-line text up to 40 characters. |
| `RelatedProduct` | string[] | product keys or aliases | optional | Must not repeat `Product`. Resolved like `Product`. |
| `Feature` | string | a feature key of the test's product | required | Custom tests: any one-line text up to 60 characters. |
| `Area` | string | an area key | required | Custom tests: any one-line text up to 60 characters. |
| `ResourceType` | string | a resource type key | required | Pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`. Custom tests may use a key that is not in the taxonomy. |
| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info` | required | unchanged |
| `UserImpact` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | required unless `Severity` is `Info` | Normalised to this spelling. |
| `ImplementationCost` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | required unless `Severity` is `Info` | Normalised to this spelling. |
| `Mitre` | string[] | `T####`, `T####.###`, or the single value `None` | required | `None` cannot be combined with an ID. IDs are validated against the pinned ATT&CK release by the build and the unit tests, not at run time. |
| `Control` | string[] | `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>` | optional; required for a test of a suite that declares `Frameworks` | Pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.\-]*:[^\s,]+$`. The requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports. It is the only way a test is mapped to a framework (section 6). Any test may use it. For a framework shipped with Maester the requirement must exist in its file. |
| `Service` | string[] | unchanged | required | |
| `License` | string[] | unchanged | optional | |
| `Permission` | string[] | `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`; `\|` joins alternatives | optional | Replaces the reserved name `GraphScope`. See section 2.4. Recorded; not enforced in 3.0. |
| `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` | string[] | unchanged | optional | |
| `Lifecycle` | string | `Preview`, `Stable`, `Deprecated` | optional, default `Stable` | Replaces `Preview`. |
| `ReplacedBy` | string | a test ID | optional | Only meaningful with `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'`. |
| `Tag` | string[] | unchanged syntax | optional | Free labels. See section 5. |
| `LongRunning`, `Exclusive`, `InstanceSource`, `Author`, `Contributor`, `HelpUrl` | | unchanged | unchanged | |

Removed properties and the error the reader gives for each:

| Property | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `Category` | "`Category` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Product` and `Feature`; the result's `Block` is derived from them." |
| `Preview` | "`Preview` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Lifecycle = 'Preview'`." |

Both are `InvalidMetadata` with that message, so a preview-era custom test fails loudly with the fix in the text.
`Convert-MtTest` writes the new form.

Reserved names become `OptionalService` and `TimeoutSeconds`. `GraphScope` and `Deprecated` are no longer
reserved: `Permission` and `Lifecycle` took their places.

### 2.2 The taxonomy registry

`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` lists the products (with their features and aliases), the areas and the
resource types. Keys are lowercase kebab-case for products, features and areas and PascalCase for resource
types. Display names live only in the registry, so a product can be renamed without touching a test.

- The reader resolves `Product` and `RelatedProduct` through `Key` and `Aliases`, case-insensitively, the same way
  service names resolve through the service registry. `Product = 'Entra ID'` therefore still loads and is stored as
  `entra`.
- For a built-in test, a `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` or `ResourceType` that is not in the registry, or a
  `Feature` that does not belong to the test's `Product`, is `InvalidMetadata`.
- For a custom test, a value that matches the registry is normalised to the key; any other value is kept as written.
- The schema table's `Products` list is removed. The order of `Products` in the registry is the order of the
  console lanes and of product lists in reports.
- `Get-MtTaxonomy` (internal) loads and caches the registry; `Get-MtTestSchema` keeps its role.

`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json` is a trimmed copy of one MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise release:
tactic and technique IDs and names, and the IDs that release retired. The registry's `Attack.Version` names the
release. `build/attack/Update-MtAttackTechniques.ps1` regenerates the file from the official STIX data when the
pin moves.

### 2.3 Derived values

Nothing in this list is typed in a test.

| Value | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `Suite`, `Source` | From the nearest `suite.json`, as today. |
| `Block` | Kept on the result row for 2.x consumers and for XML test-case names. Native tests: the display name of `Product` when it resolves in the registry; else `Product` as written; else `Feature`; else the suite's `Name`; else `Custom`. Pester-format tests: the `Describe` or `Context` name, as today. |
| Tactics | Looked up from `Mitre` in the pinned ATT&CK file when a consumer needs them. |
| Selection tags | See section 5. |

`Convert-MtTest` writes the `Describe` name of a converted Pester test to `Feature`, so its `Block`, and with it
its CI test-case name, does not change.

### 2.4 Permission

Added 2026-10-23, before any built-in test used the property. The first user is the Active Directory suite
(maester365/maester#2483); Graph scopes follow in a scripted pass.

**Grammar.** Each element is one permission, `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`, or several joined with `|`.

- `Service` is a service-registry key or alias, stored as the key. For a built-in test it must be one of the
  test's `Service` values. A custom test may name any service, for example a pack connector's.
- `Kind` is one of the kinds the registry lists for the service (`PermissionKinds` in
  `MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1`): `Scope`, `DelegatedScope`, `ApplicationScope` and `Role` for Graph; `Role` and
  `Action` for Azure; `Role` and `Cmdlet` for Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and Teams; `Ldap`, `Cim`,
  `File`, `Remoting` and `Group` for Active Directory; and so on. Each kind has an example and a description,
  which the docs and the test builder show.
- `Name` is the rest of the string after the second colon, as the product spells it. It may contain colons
  (GitHub's `administration:read`, a Google scope URL). The engine does not parse it; a suite may document a
  sub-grammar for its own kinds (Active Directory's `Ldap:[<partition>/]<objectClass>[.<attribute>]:<right>`).
- No commas, as for every list property. `|` is reserved as the separator; no permission vocabulary uses it.

**Meaning.** The identity needs every element (all-of, like `Service`). Inside an element any one alternative
is enough, and the first is the least privileged. In logic terms the list is an AND of ORs, the form in which
Microsoft documents each Graph API (one need, a least privileged permission and higher privileged ones). Any
condition can be written this way: "(A and B) or C" is `('A | C', 'B | C')`.

`License` is the other way round (the list is any-of and `&` is all-of) because a test usually needs one of
several SKUs. A test usually needs several permissions at once, and an OR of ANDs would have to list every
combination. The operator in the string always says what it means.

**Why one string and not a structured value.** The reader accepts only string constants and a C# attribute
property cannot be a hashtable. A string with a fixed prefix also matches `Control` (`<framework-key>:<id>`).

**Why not a protocol-first format.** The five-segment `<protocol>:<category>:<objectClass>:<attribute>:<right>`
form first proposed for Active Directory leaves out the service, embeds Maester's internal collector names, and
has no place for Graph scopes, roles, Azure RBAC or connector scopes. Its detail survives as the name of the
Active Directory kinds.

**Normalisation and validation.** The reader writes a registered service and kind in their registry spelling and
puts one space around each `|`. It rejects a value that does not fit the grammar, a duplicate alternative and a
duplicate element. For a built-in test it also rejects an unregistered service, a service the test does not list
and a kind the registry does not list for the service.

**What uses it.** The result row and the catalog carry the list as written. Planned, not part of this change: a
generated least-privilege page per service (the first alternative of every element of the selected tests), a
"Requires" line in the report, and a `Skipped` / `MissingPermission` reason for services where the engine can see
the identity's grants before a test runs (Graph token scopes and Entra roles, pack connector scopes; the packs
design's `MissingScope` would become this reason).

## 3. Results and catalog

Every native row gains these fields. Fields that a test does not declare are written as `null` or an empty
list, never omitted.

`Product` (now the key), `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `UserImpact`,
`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`.

`Tag` on a row holds the authored tags (plus instance tags of a family) and nothing else: no suite tags, no test
ID, no flags.

The result gains one top-level object so a consumer can render names without the module:

```json
"Taxonomy": {
  "Products":      [{ "Key": "entra", "Name": "Entra ID" }],
  "Features":      [{ "Product": "entra", "Key": "conditional-access", "Name": "Conditional Access" }],
  "Areas":         [{ "Key": "authentication", "Name": "Authentication" }],
  "ResourceTypes": [{ "Key": "Tenant" }],
  "Attack":        { "Version": "19.2", "Techniques": [{ "Id": "T1110", "Name": "Brute Force", "Tactics": ["TA0006"] }],
                     "Tactics": [{ "Id": "TA0006", "Name": "Credential Access" }] }
}
```

It lists only the keys and techniques that the rows of that result use. Pester-format rows carry the new fields
as `null`.

The built-in catalog (`Maester.TestCatalog.json`) receives the same properties through the existing generic copy,
plus the full `Taxonomy`. The build fails when a built-in test names a technique that is unknown or retired in
the pinned release.

The console keeps one lane per product. It reads the lane title and order from the registry.

## 4. Selection

`Invoke-Maester` and the `Selection` section of the run config gain typed selectors:

| Parameter | Config key | Matches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-Product` | `Selection.Product` | `Product` or any `RelatedProduct`. Aliases resolve. |
| `-Feature` | `Selection.Feature` | `Feature` |
| `-Area` | `Selection.Area` | `Area` |
| `-Severity` | `Selection.Severity` | The effective severity |
| `-Suite` | `Selection.Suite` | `Suite` |

Each takes a list. Values within one selector are alternatives; different selectors must all match, and they
combine the same way with `-Tag` and `-TestId`. `*` wildcards work as they do for tags. `Get-MtTest` takes the
same five parameters. Excluding by attribute is not added in 3.0; `-ExcludeTag` and `-ExcludeTestId` remain.

Default exclusions stop being tags:

- A test with `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` is not run unless `-IncludePreview` is given, any `-Tag` is given, or its
  exact ID is in `-TestId`. This is the 2.x rule for the `Preview` tag.
- `LongRunning` keeps its rule.
- A test whose service is opt-in in the service registry, such as Active Directory, is not run unless that
  service is connected. The `AD` tag no longer decides this.
- `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'` tests still run. The row says so, and reports may set them apart.

## 5. Tags

Built-in tests ship without taxonomy tags. `Tag` remains for labels a test owner finds useful and for custom tests.

### 5.1 Selecting with 2.x tags

`-Tag CA`, `-Tag CIS`, `-ExcludeTag MS.AAD.3.5` and every other 2.x tag string keep working for the 3.x line.

- `powershell/assets/Maester.LegacyTags.json` maps each 2.x tag to the IDs of the built-in tests that carried it.
  It is generated once from the frozen 2.x snapshot (`powershell/tests/fixtures/golden/tags-and-blocks.json`) and
  from the tags that 3.0 previews carried, and is not edited by hand afterwards. Tests added after 3.0 are not in it.
- When resolving `-Tag` and `-ExcludeTag`, a built-in test's selection tags are its authored `Tag` values, the
  `Tags` of its suite, its legacy tags from that file, and its own ID. Suite tags, legacy tags and the ID are used
  for selection only and are never written to a result row.
- A custom native test matches on its authored tags and its suite's tags. Its ID is selected with `-TestId`.
- The first time a run selects through a legacy tag, Maester writes one warning that names the tag and, where
  the file gives one, the typed selector that replaces it, for example `-Tag CA` → `-Feature conditional-access`.
- A unit test asserts that every tag in the 2.x snapshot still selects exactly the set of test IDs it selected in 2.x.

### 5.2 What replaces each kind of tag

| 2.x tag | Example | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Suite | `CISA`, `Maester` | `-Suite cisa`; `Suite` on the row |
| Product or service | `EXO`, `Entra` | `-Product exchange`; `Product` on the row |
| Topic or theme | `CA`, `AD.User`, `Privileged` | `-Feature conditional-access`, `-Area privileged-access` |
| Benchmark control ID | `MS.AAD.3.5` | `-TestId CISA.MS.AAD.3.5`; `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.5'` on the test |
| Benchmark version, level, profile | `CIS M365 v7.0.0`, `L1`, `CIS E3 Level 1` | The suite's framework file (section 6) |
| Licence | `Entra ID P1` | `License` on the row |
| Severity | `Severity:High` | `-Severity High` |
| Lifecycle | `Deprecated`, `Preview` | `Lifecycle` |

## 6. Benchmarks and framework files

A test is mapped to a framework in one place, its `Control` attribute:

```powershell
Control = 'cis-m365:5.2.2.3'
```

This is the same for a CIS or CISA test, for a Maester test that supports one of their requirements, and for a
custom test. There is no second mechanism: a framework file does not list tests, and a test's ID prefix means
nothing to the engine.

A framework file is the catalogue of a framework. A suite that holds one declares it in its `suite.json`:

```json
"Frameworks": [
  { "Key": "cis-m365", "Version": "7.0.0" }
]
```

The file is `frameworks/<key>.json` beside the `suite.json`:

```json
{
  "Framework": "cis-m365",
  "Name": "CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark",
  "Version": "7.0.0",
  "Url": "https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365",
  "Requirements": [
    { "Id": "5.2.2.3", "Level": "L1", "Profile": ["E3 Level 1"] }
  ]
}
```

It holds what a `key:id` string cannot: the name and version of the framework, the facts about each requirement
that used to be tags (level, profile, criticality, upstream status), the `Related` controls of other frameworks,
and the full list of requirements, so that a gap or a mistyped ID is found. A `Tests` key on a requirement and an
`IdPrefix` key in the declaration are ignored.

- Frameworks are looked up by key across every suite: the suites shipped with Maester and the suites under the
  user's test folder. A key that two suites declare is a problem that names both `suite.json` files.
- A row's `Benchmark` is built from the first `Control` value, in the order of the attribute, that names a
  requirement of a valid framework file: `{ "Framework": "cis-m365", "Version": "7.0.0", "Requirement": "5.2.2.3" }`
  plus the requirement's own facts. It is `null` when no value does.
- A row's `Control` list is the test's `Control` values followed by the `Related` references of every requirement
  they name, each once.
- The catalog build fails on a problem with a declaration or a file, on a key declared twice, and on a built-in
  test whose `Control` names a loaded framework and a requirement its file does not have. A run only warns.
- Reports say a test supports a control. They do not state compliance with a framework.

Framework files for CIS Microsoft 365, CIS GitHub and CISA SCuBA ship with their suites. The CISA file carries
each policy's revision, SHALL or SHOULD, and the NIST SP 800-53 mapping that ScubaGear publishes.

## 7. Enforcement

1. **Reader and build.** Section 2 rules. An invalid built-in test fails the build.
2. **Unit tests**, `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1`:
   - every built-in test has the required attributes of section 2.1;
   - every key is in the taxonomy and every feature belongs to its product;
   - `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` are absent when `Severity` is `Info` and present otherwise;
   - `Mitre` is a valid list for the pinned release, with no technique listed beside one of its own
     sub-techniques, and at most five entries;
   - no built-in test carries a tag that is a product, feature, area, suite or severity name, a benchmark label
     or a test ID;
   - a `Control` that names a framework shipped with Maester names a requirement of its file, and every test of a
     suite that declares `Frameworks` has a `Control` for a requirement of one of them;
   - the taxonomy has no unused or duplicate key, the folder of a test agrees with its `Product`, and the
     rubric's area table lists exactly the areas of the registry.

   Whether `ResourceType` should be `Tenant` cannot be decided mechanically (a test that checks that one policy
   exists may still list the policies that satisfy it), so that rule is left to the attribute review.
3. **Attribute review.** A pull request that adds a test or changes a rubric attribute is checked by a reviewer
   model against the rubric page. The check fails when a value does not fit, and reports the expected value and
   the reason. The workflow runs trusted code from the base branch only and treats the pull request's files as data.

## 8. Migration

- One script, `build/migration/Convert-MtTestAttributes.ps1`, rewrites the attribute of every built-in test:
  it drops `Category`, turns `Preview` into `Lifecycle`, writes `Product` as a key, removes the 2.x tags and
  merges the values in `build/migration/attributes/*.json` when that folder exists. It is idempotent. EIDSCA and
  ORCA take their values from their generator metadata files and are regenerated, never edited. The values files
  were removed after the migration ran; the values now live in the tests and in the generator metadata.
- The golden test stops comparing `Block` and tags with the 2.x snapshot and asserts section 5.1 instead.
- `Get-MtTestInventory`, kept for one major version, reports `Feature` where it reported the `Describe` name.

## 9. Compatibility

| Consumer | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-Tag`, `-ExcludeTag` with 2.x tags | Unchanged for built-in tests, with a warning once per run. |
| Result `Block` | Changes for built-in tests to the product name. CI test-case names of built-in tests change once. |
| Result `Tag` | Built-in rows no longer list suite, product or benchmark tags or the test ID. Use the typed fields. |
| Result `Product` | Now a key. `Taxonomy.Products` gives the name. |
| Custom native tests written for a 3.0 preview | `Category` and `Preview` are rejected with the replacement in the message. `Convert-MtTest` and `New-MtTest` write the new form. |
| Pester-format tests | No change. |

1	# Design: the Zero Trust Assessment pack
2	
3	> **Status: DRAFT.** Drafted 2026-10-19 against the Maester Packs design
4	> ([maester-packs-design.md](maester-packs-design.md), draft PR #2358) and the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment
5	> at commit `fa6ffc8` of [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment)
6	> (module version 2.6.0). The owner ruled on 2026-10-19 that the pack ships with Maester and is opt-in.
7	
8	## 1. Summary
9	
10	Maester ships an official pack, `maester.zero-trust-assessment`, that runs Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment
11	(ZTA) and shows each of its results as a Maester result row, `ZTA.<ZTA test ID>`. It lives in
12	`packs/zero-trust-assessment/`. It does not copy ZTA's code: it runs the `ZeroTrustAssessment` module the user
13	installs, or reads a report ZTA already wrote.
14	
15	- **One family test.** The pack is a single 3.0 native test, `ZTA`, whose instance source gets ZTA's
16	  report and returns one instance per result. Families already exist in 3.0, so the pack runs on today's engine

# Design: the Zero Trust Assessment pack

> **Status: DRAFT.** Drafted 2026-10-19 against the Maester Packs design
> ([maester-packs-design.md](maester-packs-design.md), draft PR #2358) and the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment
> at commit `fa6ffc8` of [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment)
> (module version 2.6.0). The owner ruled on 2026-10-19 that the pack ships with Maester and is opt-in.

## 1. Summary

Maester ships an official pack, `maester.zero-trust-assessment`, that runs Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment
(ZTA) and shows each of its results as a Maester result row, `ZTA.<ZTA test ID>`. It lives in
`packs/zero-trust-assessment/`. It does not copy ZTA's code: it runs the `ZeroTrustAssessment` module the user
installs, or reads a report ZTA already wrote.

- **One family test.** The pack is a single 3.0 native test, `ZTA`, whose instance source gets ZTA's
  report and returns one instance per result. Families already exist in 3.0, so the pack runs on today's engine
  as a custom test (`Invoke-MtTest -Path packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests`) and needs nothing from the pack
  loader beyond loading its one file.
- **Opt-in through `LongRunning`.** The family is `LongRunning`, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless the
  run names `ZTA`, sets `-IncludeLongRunning`, or turns either on in config. Its timeout is
  `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`.
- **Import or collect.** With `GlobalSettings."ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath"` set, the pack reads that report
  (the recommendation for CI). Without it, the pack runs ZTA in a child `pwsh` process and reads the report it
  writes.
- **A static catalog.** `catalog.json`, generated from the module by `build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1`, lists
  the 336 tests with title, pillar, risk level, impact, cost, service and licence, for the pack's listing.

## 2. What the Zero Trust Assessment is

ZTA is Microsoft's PowerShell module (MIT licence) that rates a Microsoft 365 tenant against its Zero Trust
guidance. 3.0 borrowed its test model, so the two are close:

| | ZTA | Maester 3.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A test | `Test-Assessment.<id>.ps1` with `[ZtTest(...)]` + `.md` | `Test.<ID>.ps1` with `[MaesterTest(...)]` + `.md` |
| Rating | `RiskLevel`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Pillar`, `Category`, `SfiPillar` | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` |
| Gates | `Service` (all-of), `CompatibleLicense`, `TenantType` | `Service`, `License`, `TenantType` |
| Result helper | `Add-ZtTestResultDetail` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail` |
| Statuses | Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error, Planned | Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error, NotRun |

The difference that decides the integration is how ZTA gets its data. `Invoke-ZtAssessment` runs in stages:
export the tenant's data (Graph, Azure, Exchange, Security & Compliance, SharePoint, AIP) into JSON files, load
them into a DuckDB database, run every test against the database with `-Database`, then write
`zt-export/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json` and an HTML report. The tests cannot run without the export and the
database, and the module carries native DuckDB binaries, PSFramework, and exact pins on the Graph, Exchange
Online and Az modules, which it downloads into its own cache and loads in a fixed MSAL order.

## 3. Options considered

| Option | What it means | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Port the tests to Maester | Rewrite 336 tests against `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` | No: they query ZTA's database, and two copies would drift |
| One Maester test per ZTA test, calling ZTA in-process | Generated `Test.ZTA.<id>.ps1` files that call ZTA's private test functions | No: needs ZTA's private functions and database, and ZTA's pinned modules cannot share a process with Maester's |
| **Run ZTA, map its report** | Run `Invoke-ZtAssessment` (or read its output) and turn each report row into a Maester row | **Chosen**: uses only ZTA's public commands and its report, which is versioned data |

Within the chosen option, the report is mapped by a family test rather than 336 generated test files. A
family runs its instance source once under its own timeout, which is exactly the "collect once, then report
many" shape ZTA needs, and it works on the 3.0 engine today. The Collect hook in the packs overview's
"Under discussion" section would give the same shape to generated per-test files; if it lands, the pack can
move to it without changing the result IDs.

## 4. How it runs

### 4.1 Import

`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` names `ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json`, the folder passed to
`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path`, or its `zt-export` folder. The pack refuses, with a skip reason on the family:

- a report for another tenant than the Graph connection (`TenantId` differs from `Get-MgContext`);
- a report older than `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` (default 7, `0` turns it off);
- a file that is missing or has no `Tests` list.

Import is text only: no ZTA code runs in the Maester process.

### 4.2 Collect

Without a report path, the pack needs `ZeroTrustAssessment` installed (Maester never installs it; the skip
reason says how). It starts the newest installed version in a child `pwsh -NoProfile` process:

1. Writes a request file with the `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` parameters, so no setting
   reaches a command line.
2. Signs the child in with `Connect-ZtAssessment`: to Maester's tenant; with Maester's app and certificate when
   Maester is connected app-only with a certificate; interactively otherwise. `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect`
   adds or overrides parameters.
3. Runs `Invoke-ZtAssessment -NoBrowser` with `Pillar`, `Tests` and `Days` from settings, telemetry off unless
   `ZeroTrustAssessment.DisableTelemetry` is `false`, and Maester's `EmergencyAccessAccounts` passed through ZTA's
   configuration file (both tools use the same shape).
4. Waits in one-second steps, so a Maester timeout or Ctrl+C stops it, and kills the child if the run stops.
5. Reads the report as in Import. The output goes to a new temporary folder that is deleted afterwards,
   because the export is raw tenant data, unless `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` is set.

The child process is why the pack's Graph scopes do not touch `Connect-Maester`: the child signs in with ZTA's
own scopes. It also means an interactive user signs in twice; CI should use Import or an app with a certificate.

### 4.3 Mapping

| ZTA | Maester |
| --- | --- |
| `TestId` | Instance suffix: `ZTA.<TestId>`. A repeated ID (the Defender for Cloud rows) gets `.<first 10 hex of SHA-256 of the title>`; exact repeats get `.2`, `.3` |
| `TestTitle` | Instance `Title` |
| `TestRisk` High, Medium, Low | Instance `Severity`; `Unranked` leaves it to config |
| `TestPillar` | Tags `ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` |
| `TestDescription`, `TestResult` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -Description -Result` |
| Passed, Failed | `$true`, `$false` |
| Investigate | `-Investigate`, `$true` |
| Skipped | Maester's own skip code where both tools have it (`NotApplicable`, the licence and connection codes), else `Custom` with ZTA's reason |
| Error, or a status the pack does not know | `-SkippedBecause Error` with ZTA's result |
| Planned (`UnderConstruction`) | Left out |

Results are taken for every ID in the report, not only the IDs in `catalog.json`, so a test added in a newer
ZTA release is reported before the catalog is regenerated. ZTA is Microsoft's code running with the user's own
consent, so the "results only for catalog IDs" rule for module packs adds nothing here.

## 5. What it needs from the packs implementation

> Checked 2026-10-19 against the loader on branch `claude/project-thread-i64voa`: `Test-MtPack -Official` passes,
> built-in packs load from `packs/<name>/` without a lock entry, `Uses.Modules` with `Install: User` and
> `Process: Child` and the `Catalog` key are accepted, and `-Suite ZTA` lifts `LongRunning`. The pack keeps the
> loader's default `EnabledByDefault: true` on purpose: `EnabledByDefault: false` would also stop `-Suite` from
> selecting it, and `LongRunning` already keeps it out of a plain run. Only the report's Packs section (item 3) is
> still open.

The pack follows the manifest of section 4.2 of the packs design and runs on the 3.0 engine, so it can land
before the loader. These are the points where the loader decides how it ships:

1. **Bundled packs.** Where official packs that ship with Maester live in the module (proposed: `packs/` in the
   module folder, copied by the build), and that they are found without `Install-MtPack` or a lock file entry,
   their integrity being the module's own.
2. **Selection.** `-Suite ZTA` should select a long-running family the way an exact `-TestId` does, so
   "turn the pack on" is one switch. Today only an exact ID or `-IncludeLongRunning` lifts `LongRunning`.
3. **The report's Packs section** should group the family's rows under the pack, with ZTA's pillar as a
   sub-group (the `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` tag).
4. **`Uses.Modules`** with `"Install": "User"` and `"Process": "Child"` is new: the module is never saved by
   Maester and never loaded in its process. The manifest schema needs both keys, or a different way to say it.
5. **`Catalog`** is a new manifest key for a static test list when a pack's tests are a family.

## 6. Open questions

- Whether Maester's own headline score should count ZTA rows (the packs design keeps pack rows out of it).
- How `Investigate` rows from ZTA (17 of 820 in Microsoft's sample report) count in the pack's pass rate.
- Overlap: Maester's MT checks and ZTA rate some of the same Entra and Intune settings (the attribute rubric
  already cross-references ZTA). A later version could link the overlapping IDs.

1	# Design: test attributes in Maester 3.0
2	
3	Status: accepted for implementation, 2026-10-11. This document replaces the `Category`, `Preview` and tag rules of
4	the [3.0 design](./maester-3.0-design.md) (sections 3.2, 4 and 7.1). Everything else in that design stands.
5	
6	## 1. Summary
7	
8	In 2.x and in the first 3.0 previews a test was described by one free-text `Category` and a list of free-form
9	tags. Between them they carried eight different ideas: suite, product, topic, benchmark control, benchmark
10	version, licence, severity and theme. Neither could drive a clean report filter, and a new idea meant a new tag
11	convention.
12	
13	This design gives each idea its own typed attribute, drawn from a closed list where a list makes sense, and
14	stops using tags for Maester's own taxonomy. A test answers six questions:
15	
16	| Question | Attributes |
17	| --- | --- |
18	| Which test is this? | `Id`, `Title` |
19	| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` |
20	| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` |
21	| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` |
22	| Can it run here? | `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` |
23	| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` |
24	
25	`Category` and `Preview` are removed. `Tag` stays as a free label for the owner of a test folder and no longer
26	carries taxonomy. The rules for choosing each value are in the
27	[attribute rubric](../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md); this document specifies the mechanics.
28	
29	## 2. The attribute
30	
31	```powershell
32	[MaesterTest(
33	    Id                 = 'MT.1012',
34	    Title              = 'MFA is required for risky sign-ins',
35	
36	    Product            = 'entra',
37	    Feature            = 'conditional-access',
38	    Area               = 'authentication',
39	    ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
40	
41	    Severity           = 'High',
42	    UserImpact         = 'Low',
43	    ImplementationCost = 'Low',
44	
45	    Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),
46	
47	    Service            = 'Graph',
48	    License            = 'AAD_PREMIUM_P2',
49	    Author             = 'f-bader'
50	)]
51	```
52	
53	### 2.1 Properties
54	
55	Types stay within what the AST reader accepts: `string`, `string[]` and `bool`.
56	
57	| Property | Type | Values | Built-in tests | Notes |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| `Id` | string | unchanged | required | |
60	| `Title` | string | unchanged | required | |
61	| `Product` | string | a product key or alias from the taxonomy | required | Stored and written to results as the key. Custom tests may use any one-line text up to 40 characters. |
62	| `RelatedProduct` | string[] | product keys or aliases | optional | Must not repeat `Product`. Resolved like `Product`. |
63	| `Feature` | string | a feature key of the test's product | required | Custom tests: any one-line text up to 60 characters. |
64	| `Area` | string | an area key | required | Custom tests: any one-line text up to 60 characters. |
65	| `ResourceType` | string | a resource type key | required | Pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`. Custom tests may use a key that is not in the taxonomy. |
66	| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info` | required | unchanged |
67	| `UserImpact` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | required unless `Severity` is `Info` | Normalised to this spelling. |
68	| `ImplementationCost` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | required unless `Severity` is `Info` | Normalised to this spelling. |
69	| `Mitre` | string[] | `T####`, `T####.###`, or the single value `None` | required | `None` cannot be combined with an ID. IDs are validated against the pinned ATT&CK release by the build and the unit tests, not at run time. |
70	| `Control` | string[] | `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>` | optional; required for a test of a suite that declares `Frameworks` | Pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.\-]*:[^\s,]+$`. The requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports. It is the only way a test is mapped to a framework (section 6). Any test may use it. For a framework shipped with Maester the requirement must exist in its file. |
71	| `Service` | string[] | unchanged | required | |
72	| `License` | string[] | unchanged | optional | |
73	| `Permission` | string[] | `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`; `\|` joins alternatives | optional | Replaces the reserved name `GraphScope`. See section 2.4. Recorded; not enforced in 3.0. |
74	| `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform` | string[] | unchanged | optional | |
75	| `Lifecycle` | string | `Preview`, `Stable`, `Deprecated` | optional, default `Stable` | Replaces `Preview`. |
76	| `ReplacedBy` | string | a test ID | optional | Only meaningful with `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'`. |
77	| `Tag` | string[] | unchanged syntax | optional | Free labels. See section 5. |
78	| `LongRunning`, `Exclusive`, `InstanceSource`, `Author`, `Contributor`, `HelpUrl` | | unchanged | unchanged | |
79	
80	Removed properties and the error the reader gives for each:
81	
82	| Property | Message |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| `Category` | "`Category` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Product` and `Feature`; the result's `Block` is derived from them." |
85	| `Preview` | "`Preview` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Lifecycle = 'Preview'`." |
86	
87	Both are `InvalidMetadata` with that message, so a preview-era custom test fails loudly with the fix in the text.
88	`Convert-MtTest` writes the new form.
89	
90	Reserved names become `OptionalService` and `TimeoutSeconds`. `GraphScope` and `Deprecated` are no longer
91	reserved: `Permission` and `Lifecycle` took their places.
92	
93	### 2.2 The taxonomy registry
94	
95	`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` lists the products (with their features and aliases), the areas and the
96	resource types. Keys are lowercase kebab-case for products, features and areas and PascalCase for resource
97	types. Display names live only in the registry, so a product can be renamed without touching a test.
98	
99	- The reader resolves `Product` and `RelatedProduct` through `Key` and `Aliases`, case-insensitively, the same way
100	  service names resolve through the service registry. `Product = 'Entra ID'` therefore still loads and is stored as
101	  `entra`.
102	- For a built-in test, a `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` or `ResourceType` that is not in the registry, or a
103	  `Feature` that does not belong to the test's `Product`, is `InvalidMetadata`.
104	- For a custom test, a value that matches the registry is normalised to the key; any other value is kept as written.
105	- The schema table's `Products` list is removed. The order of `Products` in the registry is the order of the
106	  console lanes and of product lists in reports.
107	- `Get-MtTaxonomy` (internal) loads and caches the registry; `Get-MtTestSchema` keeps its role.
108	
109	`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json` is a trimmed copy of one MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise release:
110	tactic and technique IDs and names, and the IDs that release retired. The registry's `Attack.Version` names the
111	release. `build/attack/Update-MtAttackTechniques.ps1` regenerates the file from the official STIX data when the
112	pin moves.
113	
114	### 2.3 Derived values
115	
116	Nothing in this list is typed in a test.
117	
118	| Value | Rule |
119	| --- | --- |
120	| `Suite`, `Source` | From the nearest `suite.json`, as today. |
121	| `Block` | Kept on the result row for 2.x consumers and for XML test-case names. Native tests: the display name of `Product` when it resolves in the registry; else `Product` as written; else `Feature`; else the suite's `Name`; else `Custom`. Pester-format tests: the `Describe` or `Context` name, as today. |
122	| Tactics | Looked up from `Mitre` in the pinned ATT&CK file when a consumer needs them. |
123	| Selection tags | See section 5. |
124	
125	`Convert-MtTest` writes the `Describe` name of a converted Pester test to `Feature`, so its `Block`, and with it
126	its CI test-case name, does not change.
127	
128	### 2.4 Permission
129	
130	Added 2026-10-23, before any built-in test used the property. The first user is the Active Directory suite
131	(maester365/maester#2483); Graph scopes follow in a scripted pass.
132	
133	**Grammar.** Each element is one permission, `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`, or several joined with `|`.
134	
135	- `Service` is a service-registry key or alias, stored as the key. For a built-in test it must be one of the
136	  test's `Service` values. A custom test may name any service, for example a pack connector's.
137	- `Kind` is one of the kinds the registry lists for the service (`PermissionKinds` in
138	  `MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1`): `Scope`, `DelegatedScope`, `ApplicationScope` and `Role` for Graph; `Role` and
139	  `Action` for Azure; `Role` and `Cmdlet` for Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and Teams; `Ldap`, `Cim`,
140	  `File`, `Remoting` and `Group` for Active Directory; and so on. Each kind has an example and a description,
141	  which the docs and the test builder show.
142	- `Name` is the rest of the string after the second colon, as the product spells it. It may contain colons
143	  (GitHub's `administration:read`, a Google scope URL). The engine does not parse it; a suite may document a
144	  sub-grammar for its own kinds (Active Directory's `Ldap:[<partition>/]<objectClass>[.<attribute>]:<right>`).
145	- No commas, as for every list property. `|` is reserved as the separator; no permission vocabulary uses it.
146	
147	**Meaning.** The identity needs every element (all-of, like `Service`). Inside an element any one alternative
148	is enough, and the first is the least privileged. In logic terms the list is an AND of ORs, the form in which
149	Microsoft documents each Graph API (one need, a least privileged permission and higher privileged ones). Any
150	condition can be written this way: "(A and B) or C" is `('A | C', 'B | C')`.
151	
152	`License` is the other way round (the list is any-of and `&` is all-of) because a test usually needs one of
153	several SKUs. A test usually needs several permissions at once, and an OR of ANDs would have to list every
154	combination. The operator in the string always says what it means.
155	
156	**Why one string and not a structured value.** The reader accepts only string constants and a C# attribute
157	property cannot be a hashtable. A string with a fixed prefix also matches `Control` (`<framework-key>:<id>`).
158	
159	**Why not a protocol-first format.** The five-segment `<protocol>:<category>:<objectClass>:<attribute>:<right>`
160	form first proposed for Active Directory leaves out the service, embeds Maester's internal collector names, and
161	has no place for Graph scopes, roles, Azure RBAC or connector scopes. Its detail survives as the name of the
162	Active Directory kinds.
163	
164	**Normalisation and validation.** The reader writes a registered service and kind in their registry spelling and
165	puts one space around each `|`. It rejects a value that does not fit the grammar, a duplicate alternative and a
166	duplicate element. For a built-in test it also rejects an unregistered service, a service the test does not list
167	and a kind the registry does not list for the service.
168	
169	**What uses it.** The result row and the catalog carry the list as written. Planned, not part of this change: a
170	generated least-privilege page per service (the first alternative of every element of the selected tests), a
171	"Requires" line in the report, and a `Skipped` / `MissingPermission` reason for services where the engine can see
172	the identity's grants before a test runs (Graph token scopes and Entra roles, pack connector scopes; the packs
173	design's `MissingScope` would become this reason).
174	
175	## 3. Results and catalog
176	
177	Every native row gains these fields. Fields that a test does not declare are written as `null` or an empty
178	list, never omitted.
179	
180	`Product` (now the key), `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `UserImpact`,
181	`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`.
182	
183	`Tag` on a row holds the authored tags (plus instance tags of a family) and nothing else: no suite tags, no test
184	ID, no flags.
185	
186	The result gains one top-level object so a consumer can render names without the module:
187	
188	```json
189	"Taxonomy": {
190	  "Products":      [{ "Key": "entra", "Name": "Entra ID" }],
191	  "Features":      [{ "Product": "entra", "Key": "conditional-access", "Name": "Conditional Access" }],
192	  "Areas":         [{ "Key": "authentication", "Name": "Authentication" }],
193	  "ResourceTypes": [{ "Key": "Tenant" }],
194	  "Attack":        { "Version": "19.2", "Techniques": [{ "Id": "T1110", "Name": "Brute Force", "Tactics": ["TA0006"] }],
195	                     "Tactics": [{ "Id": "TA0006", "Name": "Credential Access" }] }
196	}
197	```
198	
199	It lists only the keys and techniques that the rows of that result use. Pester-format rows carry the new fields
200	as `null`.
201	
202	The built-in catalog (`Maester.TestCatalog.json`) receives the same properties through the existing generic copy,
203	plus the full `Taxonomy`. The build fails when a built-in test names a technique that is unknown or retired in
204	the pinned release.
205	
206	The console keeps one lane per product. It reads the lane title and order from the registry.
207	
208	## 4. Selection
209	
210	`Invoke-Maester` and the `Selection` section of the run config gain typed selectors:
211	
212	| Parameter | Config key | Matches |
213	| --- | --- | --- |
214	| `-Product` | `Selection.Product` | `Product` or any `RelatedProduct`. Aliases resolve. |
215	| `-Feature` | `Selection.Feature` | `Feature` |
216	| `-Area` | `Selection.Area` | `Area` |
217	| `-Severity` | `Selection.Severity` | The effective severity |
218	| `-Suite` | `Selection.Suite` | `Suite` |
219	
220	Each takes a list. Values within one selector are alternatives; different selectors must all match, and they
221	combine the same way with `-Tag` and `-TestId`. `*` wildcards work as they do for tags. `Get-MtTest` takes the
222	same five parameters. Excluding by attribute is not added in 3.0; `-ExcludeTag` and `-ExcludeTestId` remain.
223	
224	Default exclusions stop being tags:
225	
226	- A test with `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` is not run unless `-IncludePreview` is given, any `-Tag` is given, or its
227	  exact ID is in `-TestId`. This is the 2.x rule for the `Preview` tag.
228	- `LongRunning` keeps its rule.
229	- A test whose service is opt-in in the service registry, such as Active Directory, is not run unless that
230	  service is connected. The `AD` tag no longer decides this.
231	- `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'` tests still run. The row says so, and reports may set them apart.
232	
233	## 5. Tags
234	
235	Built-in tests ship without taxonomy tags. `Tag` remains for labels a test owner finds useful and for custom tests.
236	
237	### 5.1 Selecting with 2.x tags
238	
239	`-Tag CA`, `-Tag CIS`, `-ExcludeTag MS.AAD.3.5` and every other 2.x tag string keep working for the 3.x line.
240	
241	- `powershell/assets/Maester.LegacyTags.json` maps each 2.x tag to the IDs of the built-in tests that carried it.
242	  It is generated once from the frozen 2.x snapshot (`powershell/tests/fixtures/golden/tags-and-blocks.json`) and
243	  from the tags that 3.0 previews carried, and is not edited by hand afterwards. Tests added after 3.0 are not in it.
244	- When resolving `-Tag` and `-ExcludeTag`, a built-in test's selection tags are its authored `Tag` values, the
245	  `Tags` of its suite, its legacy tags from that file, and its own ID. Suite tags, legacy tags and the ID are used
246	  for selection only and are never written to a result row.
247	- A custom native test matches on its authored tags and its suite's tags. Its ID is selected with `-TestId`.
248	- The first time a run selects through a legacy tag, Maester writes one warning that names the tag and, where
249	  the file gives one, the typed selector that replaces it, for example `-Tag CA` → `-Feature conditional-access`.
250	- A unit test asserts that every tag in the 2.x snapshot still selects exactly the set of test IDs it selected in 2.x.
251	
252	### 5.2 What replaces each kind of tag
253	
254	| 2.x tag | Example | Now |
255	| --- | --- | --- |
256	| Suite | `CISA`, `Maester` | `-Suite cisa`; `Suite` on the row |
257	| Product or service | `EXO`, `Entra` | `-Product exchange`; `Product` on the row |
258	| Topic or theme | `CA`, `AD.User`, `Privileged` | `-Feature conditional-access`, `-Area privileged-access` |
259	| Benchmark control ID | `MS.AAD.3.5` | `-TestId CISA.MS.AAD.3.5`; `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.5'` on the test |
260	| Benchmark version, level, profile | `CIS M365 v7.0.0`, `L1`, `CIS E3 Level 1` | The suite's framework file (section 6) |
261	| Licence | `Entra ID P1` | `License` on the row |
262	| Severity | `Severity:High` | `-Severity High` |
263	| Lifecycle | `Deprecated`, `Preview` | `Lifecycle` |
264	
265	## 6. Benchmarks and framework files
266	
267	A test is mapped to a framework in one place, its `Control` attribute:
268	
269	```powershell
270	Control = 'cis-m365:5.2.2.3'
271	```
272	
273	This is the same for a CIS or CISA test, for a Maester test that supports one of their requirements, and for a
274	custom test. There is no second mechanism: a framework file does not list tests, and a test's ID prefix means
275	nothing to the engine.
276	
277	A framework file is the catalogue of a framework. A suite that holds one declares it in its `suite.json`:
278	
279	```json
280	"Frameworks": [
281	  { "Key": "cis-m365", "Version": "7.0.0" }
282	]
283	```
284	
285	The file is `frameworks/<key>.json` beside the `suite.json`:
286	
287	```json
288	{
289	  "Framework": "cis-m365",
290	  "Name": "CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark",
291	  "Version": "7.0.0",
292	  "Url": "https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365",
293	  "Requirements": [
294	    { "Id": "5.2.2.3", "Level": "L1", "Profile": ["E3 Level 1"] }
295	  ]
296	}
297	```
298	
299	It holds what a `key:id` string cannot: the name and version of the framework, the facts about each requirement
300	that used to be tags (level, profile, criticality, upstream status), the `Related` controls of other frameworks,
301	and the full list of requirements, so that a gap or a mistyped ID is found. A `Tests` key on a requirement and an
302	`IdPrefix` key in the declaration are ignored.
303	
304	- Frameworks are looked up by key across every suite: the suites shipped with Maester and the suites under the
305	  user's test folder. A key that two suites declare is a problem that names both `suite.json` files.
306	- A row's `Benchmark` is built from the first `Control` value, in the order of the attribute, that names a
307	  requirement of a valid framework file: `{ "Framework": "cis-m365", "Version": "7.0.0", "Requirement": "5.2.2.3" }`
308	  plus the requirement's own facts. It is `null` when no value does.
309	- A row's `Control` list is the test's `Control` values followed by the `Related` references of every requirement
310	  they name, each once.
311	- The catalog build fails on a problem with a declaration or a file, on a key declared twice, and on a built-in
312	  test whose `Control` names a loaded framework and a requirement its file does not have. A run only warns.
313	- Reports say a test supports a control. They do not state compliance with a framework.
314	
315	Framework files for CIS Microsoft 365, CIS GitHub and CISA SCuBA ship with their suites. The CISA file carries
316	each policy's revision, SHALL or SHOULD, and the NIST SP 800-53 mapping that ScubaGear publishes.
317	
318	## 7. Enforcement
319	
320	1. **Reader and build.** Section 2 rules. An invalid built-in test fails the build.
321	2. **Unit tests**, `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1`:
322	   - every built-in test has the required attributes of section 2.1;
323	   - every key is in the taxonomy and every feature belongs to its product;
324	   - `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` are absent when `Severity` is `Info` and present otherwise;
325	   - `Mitre` is a valid list for the pinned release, with no technique listed beside one of its own
326	     sub-techniques, and at most five entries;
327	   - no built-in test carries a tag that is a product, feature, area, suite or severity name, a benchmark label
328	     or a test ID;
329	   - a `Control` that names a framework shipped with Maester names a requirement of its file, and every test of a
330	     suite that declares `Frameworks` has a `Control` for a requirement of one of them;
331	   - the taxonomy has no unused or duplicate key, the folder of a test agrees with its `Product`, and the
332	     rubric's area table lists exactly the areas of the registry.
333	
334	   Whether `ResourceType` should be `Tenant` cannot be decided mechanically (a test that checks that one policy
335	   exists may still list the policies that satisfy it), so that rule is left to the attribute review.
336	3. **Attribute review.** A pull request that adds a test or changes a rubric attribute is checked by a reviewer
337	   model against the rubric page. The check fails when a value does not fit, and reports the expected value and
338	   the reason. The workflow runs trusted code from the base branch only and treats the pull request's files as data.
339	
340	## 8. Migration
341	
342	- One script, `build/migration/Convert-MtTestAttributes.ps1`, rewrites the attribute of every built-in test:
343	  it drops `Category`, turns `Preview` into `Lifecycle`, writes `Product` as a key, removes the 2.x tags and
344	  merges the values in `build/migration/attributes/*.json` when that folder exists. It is idempotent. EIDSCA and
345	  ORCA take their values from their generator metadata files and are regenerated, never edited. The values files
346	  were removed after the migration ran; the values now live in the tests and in the generator metadata.
347	- The golden test stops comparing `Block` and tags with the 2.x snapshot and asserts section 5.1 instead.
348	- `Get-MtTestInventory`, kept for one major version, reports `Feature` where it reported the `Describe` name.
349	
350	## 9. Compatibility
351	
352	| Consumer | Effect |
353	| --- | --- |
354	| `-Tag`, `-ExcludeTag` with 2.x tags | Unchanged for built-in tests, with a warning once per run. |
355	| Result `Block` | Changes for built-in tests to the product name. CI test-case names of built-in tests change once. |
356	| Result `Tag` | Built-in rows no longer list suite, product or benchmark tags or the test ID. Use the typed fields. |
357	| Result `Product` | Now a key. `Taxonomy.Products` gives the name. |
358	| Custom native tests written for a 3.0 preview | `Category` and `Preview` are rejected with the replacement in the message. `Convert-MtTest` and `New-MtTest` write the new form. |
359	| Pester-format tests | No change. |
