1	# Design: the Zero Trust Assessment pack
2	
3	> **Status: DRAFT.** Drafted 2026-10-19 against the Maester Packs design
4	> ([maester-packs-design.md](maester-packs-design.md), draft PR #2358) and the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment
5	> at commit `fa6ffc8` of [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment)
6	> (module version 2.6.0). The owner ruled on 2026-10-19 that the pack ships with Maester and is opt-in.
7	
8	## 1. Summary
9	
10	Maester ships an official pack, `maester.zero-trust-assessment`, that runs Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment
11	(ZTA) and shows each of its results as a Maester result row, `ZTA.<ZTA test ID>`. It lives in
12	`packs/zero-trust-assessment/`. It does not copy ZTA's code: it runs the `ZeroTrustAssessment` module the user
13	installs, or reads a report ZTA already wrote.
14	
15	- **One family test.** The pack is a single 3.0 native test, `ZTA`, whose instance source gets ZTA's
16	  report and returns one instance per result. Families already exist in 3.0, so the pack runs on today's engine
17	  as a custom test (`Invoke-MtTest -Path packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests`) and needs nothing from the pack
18	  loader beyond loading its one file.
19	- **Opt-in through `LongRunning`.** The family is `LongRunning`, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless the
20	  run names `ZTA`, sets `-IncludeLongRunning`, or turns either on in config. Its timeout is
21	  `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`.
22	- **Import or collect.** With `GlobalSettings."ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath"` set, the pack reads that report
23	  (the recommendation for CI). Without it, the pack runs ZTA in a child `pwsh` process and reads the report it
24	  writes.
25	- **A static catalog.** `catalog.json`, generated from the module by `build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1`, lists
26	  the 336 tests with title, pillar, risk level, impact, cost, service and licence, for the pack's listing.
27	
28	## 2. What the Zero Trust Assessment is
29	
30	ZTA is Microsoft's PowerShell module (MIT licence) that rates a Microsoft 365 tenant against its Zero Trust
31	guidance. 3.0 borrowed its test model, so the two are close:
32	
33	| | ZTA | Maester 3.0 |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| A test | `Test-Assessment.<id>.ps1` with `[ZtTest(...)]` + `.md` | `Test.<ID>.ps1` with `[MaesterTest(...)]` + `.md` |
36	| Rating | `RiskLevel`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Pillar`, `Category`, `SfiPillar` | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` |
37	| Gates | `Service` (all-of), `CompatibleLicense`, `TenantType` | `Service`, `License`, `TenantType` |
38	| Result helper | `Add-ZtTestResultDetail` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail` |
39	| Statuses | Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error, Planned | Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error, NotRun |
40	
41	The difference that decides the integration is how ZTA gets its data. `Invoke-ZtAssessment` runs in stages:
42	export the tenant's data (Graph, Azure, Exchange, Security & Compliance, SharePoint, AIP) into JSON files, load
43	them into a DuckDB database, run every test against the database with `-Database`, then write
44	`zt-export/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json` and an HTML report. The tests cannot run without the export and the
45	database, and the module carries native DuckDB binaries, PSFramework, and exact pins on the Graph, Exchange
46	Online and Az modules, which it downloads into its own cache and loads in a fixed MSAL order.
47	
48	## 3. Options considered
49	
50	| Option | What it means | Verdict |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| Port the tests to Maester | Rewrite 336 tests against `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` | No: they query ZTA's database, and two copies would drift |
53	| One Maester test per ZTA test, calling ZTA in-process | Generated `Test.ZTA.<id>.ps1` files that call ZTA's private test functions | No: needs ZTA's private functions and database, and ZTA's pinned modules cannot share a process with Maester's |
54	| **Run ZTA, map its report** | Run `Invoke-ZtAssessment` (or read its output) and turn each report row into a Maester row | **Chosen**: uses only ZTA's public commands and its report, which is versioned data |
55	
56	Within the chosen option, the report is mapped by a family test rather than 336 generated test files. A
57	family runs its instance source once under its own timeout, which is exactly the "collect once, then report
58	many" shape ZTA needs, and it works on the 3.0 engine today. The Collect hook in the packs overview's
59	"Under discussion" section would give the same shape to generated per-test files; if it lands, the pack can
60	move to it without changing the result IDs.
61	
62	## 4. How it runs
63	
64	### 4.1 Import
65	
66	`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` names `ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json`, the folder passed to
67	`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path`, or its `zt-export` folder. The pack refuses, with a skip reason on the family:
68	
69	- a report for another tenant than the Graph connection (`TenantId` differs from `Get-MgContext`);
70	- a report older than `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` (default 7, `0` turns it off);
71	- a file that is missing or has no `Tests` list.
72	
73	Import is text only: no ZTA code runs in the Maester process.
74	
75	### 4.2 Collect
76	
77	Without a report path, the pack needs `ZeroTrustAssessment` installed (Maester never installs it; the skip
78	reason says how). It starts the newest installed version in a child `pwsh -NoProfile` process:
79	
80	1. Writes a request file with the `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` parameters, so no setting
81	   reaches a command line.
82	2. Signs the child in with `Connect-ZtAssessment`: to Maester's tenant; with Maester's app and certificate when
83	   Maester is connected app-only with a certificate; interactively otherwise. `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect`
84	   adds or overrides parameters.
85	3. Runs `Invoke-ZtAssessment -NoBrowser` with `Pillar`, `Tests` and `Days` from settings, telemetry off unless
86	   `ZeroTrustAssessment.DisableTelemetry` is `false`, and Maester's `EmergencyAccessAccounts` passed through ZTA's
87	   configuration file (both tools use the same shape).
88	4. Waits in one-second steps, so a Maester timeout or Ctrl+C stops it, and kills the child if the run stops.
89	5. Reads the report as in Import. The output goes to a new temporary folder that is deleted afterwards,
90	   because the export is raw tenant data, unless `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` is set.
91	
92	The child process is why the pack's Graph scopes do not touch `Connect-Maester`: the child signs in with ZTA's
93	own scopes. It also means an interactive user signs in twice; CI should use Import or an app with a certificate.
94	
95	### 4.3 Mapping
96	
97	| ZTA | Maester |
98	| --- | --- |
99	| `TestId` | Instance suffix: `ZTA.<TestId>`. A repeated ID (the Defender for Cloud rows) gets `.<first 10 hex of SHA-256 of the title>`; exact repeats get `.2`, `.3` |
100	| `TestTitle` | Instance `Title` |
101	| `TestRisk` High, Medium, Low | Instance `Severity`; `Unranked` leaves it to config |
102	| `TestPillar` | Tags `ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` |
103	| `TestDescription`, `TestResult` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -Description -Result` |
104	| Passed, Failed | `$true`, `$false` |
105	| Investigate | `-Investigate`, `$true` |
106	| Skipped | Maester's own skip code where both tools have it (`NotApplicable`, the licence and connection codes), else `Custom` with ZTA's reason |
107	| Error, or a status the pack does not know | `-SkippedBecause Error` with ZTA's result |
108	| Planned (`UnderConstruction`) | Left out |
109	
110	Results are taken for every ID in the report, not only the IDs in `catalog.json`, so a test added in a newer
111	ZTA release is reported before the catalog is regenerated. ZTA is Microsoft's code running with the user's own
112	consent, so the "results only for catalog IDs" rule for module packs adds nothing here.
113	
114	## 5. What it needs from the packs implementation
115	
116	> Checked 2026-10-19 against the loader on branch `claude/project-thread-i64voa`: `Test-MtPack -Official` passes,
117	> built-in packs load from `packs/<name>/` without a lock entry, `Uses.Modules` with `Install: User` and
118	> `Process: Child` and the `Catalog` key are accepted, and `-Suite ZTA` lifts `LongRunning`. The pack keeps the
119	> loader's default `EnabledByDefault: true` on purpose: `EnabledByDefault: false` would also stop `-Suite` from
120	> selecting it, and `LongRunning` already keeps it out of a plain run. Only the report's Packs section (item 3) is
121	> still open.
122	
123	The pack follows the manifest of section 4.2 of the packs design and runs on the 3.0 engine, so it can land
124	before the loader. These are the points where the loader decides how it ships:
125	
126	1. **Bundled packs.** Where official packs that ship with Maester live in the module (proposed: `packs/` in the
127	   module folder, copied by the build), and that they are found without `Install-MtPack` or a lock file entry,
128	   their integrity being the module's own.
129	2. **Selection.** `-Suite ZTA` should select a long-running family the way an exact `-TestId` does, so
130	   "turn the pack on" is one switch. Today only an exact ID or `-IncludeLongRunning` lifts `LongRunning`.
131	3. **The report's Packs section** should group the family's rows under the pack, with ZTA's pillar as a
132	   sub-group (the `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` tag).
133	4. **`Uses.Modules`** with `"Install": "User"` and `"Process": "Child"` is new: the module is never saved by
134	   Maester and never loaded in its process. The manifest schema needs both keys, or a different way to say it.
135	5. **`Catalog`** is a new manifest key for a static test list when a pack's tests are a family.
136	
137	## 6. Open questions
138	
139	- Whether Maester's own headline score should count ZTA rows (the packs design keeps pack rows out of it).
140	- How `Investigate` rows from ZTA (17 of 820 in Microsoft's sample report) count in the pack's pass rate.
141	- Overlap: Maester's MT checks and ZTA rate some of the same Entra and Intune settings (the attribute rubric
142	  already cross-references ZTA). A later version could link the overlapping IDs.
143

Maester's strong point Do this first: implementation order 
 Attack-path tools (Exposure Management, BloodHound, EntraHound) show the route an attacker takes. None of them show the order a defender has to work in. Microsoft Learn does, page by page, and the report ignores it today. Three examples: 
 Compliant devices Learn warns that the CA policy won't work as intended without an Intune compliance policy. It says to create one first and have at least one compliant device. Learn 
 Risk policies Users must be registered for MFA, and synced users need password writeback, or the policy blocks them. Investigate and remediate existing risk before you turn it on. Learn 
 Token protection Needs Windows devices that are Entra joined, hybrid joined or registered, and Apple devices that are MDM-managed with the SSO plug-in. Start with a pilot in report-only. Learn 
 The risk today: the action plan ranks by severity, user impact and effort. In a tenant with no compliance policies it can put MT.1001 near the top, and following that advice locks users out. The guide for MT.1001 says only "Review the configuration described above." 
 A first pass: seven chains 
 Chain Order of changes Checks that map to it Prerequisites Maester can't check yet 
 Require compliant devices Devices Entra or hybrid joined → enrolled in Intune → a compliance policy for each platform → emergency access excluded → CA requires a compliant device About 28: MT.1001 , MT.1014 , MT.1054 , MT.1188 , MT.1214 , MT.1228 – MT.1237 , CIS.M365.4.1 , 4.2 , 5.2.2.9 , 5.2.2.10 , CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 , 3.8 , ZTA.24541 – 24547 , ZTA.24824 Share of Windows devices joined; share of devices enrolled 
 Risk-based Conditional Access MFA registered, plus password writeback for synced users → existing high-risk users remediated → separate user-risk and sign-in-risk policies 9: MT.1012 , MT.1013 , MT.1049 , MT.1260 , CIS.M365.5.2.2.6 , 5.2.2.7 , CISA.MS.AAD.2.1 , 2.3 , and CIS.M365.5.1.8.1 (password hash sync feeds leaked-credential detection) MFA registration coverage; password writeback 
 Phishing-resistant MFA Passkeys, FIDO2 or Windows Hello enabled, with a Temporary Access Pass to get started → users register → enforce for admins → enforce for everyone 18: EIDSCA.AF01 – AF06 , AT01 , AT02 , ZTA.21839 , 24551 , 21782 , 21781 , 21783 , 21784 , CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 , 3.1 , 3.2 (the interim step), ASD.ISM-1872 Registration coverage for all users (ZTA checks admins only) 
 Standing privilege to PIM Emergency access kept permanent → roles made eligible → PIM alerts → eligible roles actually used 9: MT.1025 – MT.1028 , MT.1031 , MT.1030 , ZTA.21816 , 21876 , CISA.MS.AAD.7.7 None 
 Token protection Devices joined or registered (shared with the first chain) → pilot in report-only → enforce 3: CIS.M365.5.2.2.16 , ZTA.21941 , ZTA.21786 Device join coverage 
 Email authentication SPF and DKIM → DMARC at p=none with reports → p=reject 12: CIS.M365.2.1.8 , 2.1.9 , 2.1.10 , CISA.MS.EXO.2.2 , 3.1 , 4.1 – 4.3 , ORCA.108 , 108.1 , 235 , MT.1182 None 
 Defender risk in compliance Devices onboarded to Defender for Endpoint → Defender connected to Intune → compliance policies require a risk level 5: ZTA.41045 , ZTA.24871 , MT.1216 , MT.1231 , MT.1235 The Defender connector in Intune 
 Three foundation changes sit under most chains: emergency access accounts excluded and not blocked ( MT.1005 , MT.1034 ), and directory sync accounts excluded in hybrid tenants ( MT.1020 ). The pass also turned up six prerequisites Maester has no check for. They are candidates for readiness checks that report a share, such as 71% of devices enrolled. 
 Where the seven chains came from 
 I chose them by hand. They're the deployments where Microsoft's guidance is most explicit about order, and where the wrong order locks users out. I matched each against the titles of Maester's 893 checks and the Zero Trust pack's catalogue. Three were confirmed against Microsoft Learn in this research: compliant devices, risk policies and token protection. The other four (PIM, phishing-resistant MFA, email authentication and Defender risk) come from Microsoft guidance I know and still need the same check. Treat the table as a worked example, not a finished catalogue. 
 More chains to look at 
 Chain Order of changes Checks that map to it 
 Block legacy authentication Find legacy sign-ins → move clients to modern auth → block in CA MT.1009 , MT.1010 , MT.1033 , plus measured impact (B1) 
 Guest and external access Entra B2B and cross-tenant settings → Microsoft 365 Groups guest settings → Teams guest access → SharePoint organisation sharing → site sharing (a site can't be more open than the organisation) → MFA for guests → access reviews MT.1016 , ZTA.21857 , EIDSCA authorization settings, Teams and SharePoint sharing checks 
 App consent Admin consent workflow → restrict user consent → review existing grants EIDSCA.AP09 , EIDSCA.CP03 , CIS consent checks 
 Workload credentials Certificates, managed identities or federated credentials → remove secrets → limit credential lifetimes → app owners have MFA, or privileged apps have no owners MT.1057 , MT.1198 , MT.1199 , MT.1063 , MT.1077 , MT.1078 
 Hybrid identity hardening Password hash sync → block soft and hard matching → turn off seamless SSO → cloud-only admins CIS.M365.5.1.8.1 , MT.1073 , MT.1084 , MT.1026 , MT.1081 , MT.1147 
 Self-service password reset SSPR → password writeback → feeds remediation in the risk chain None found by title: a gap 
 Local admin and LAPS Entra join → LAPS → limit local admins at join → restrict BitLocker key recovery CIS.M365.5.1.4.3 – 5.1.4.6 , MT.1090 , MT.1091 , ZTA.21955 
 Data protection Sensitivity labels for groups and sites → publish labels → default and automatic labels → DLP in simulation → enforce The 10 Purview checks 
 SharePoint sharing Tenant sharing level → anyone links off or expiring → default link type → site overrides The 20 SharePoint checks 
 Audit and detection Unified audit log → mailbox auditing → alert policies → diagnostic settings to a SIEM MT.1172 , MT.1100 . Maester's own log reads (B1, B2) depend on this chain too. 
 Defender for Office 365 Preset policies → priority accounts → impersonation protection ZTA.41033 and ORCA checks. Needs a VIP list, which C1 could suggest. 
 Global Secure Access Devices joined or registered → client deployed → traffic forwarding profiles → Global Secure Access signalling for CA → compliant network in CA; tenant restrictions v2 → universal tenant restrictions; private access apps behind CA with a managed device ZTA.25372 , MT.1187 , MT.1189 , ZTA.25379 , MT.1188 , MT.1193 
 AI agents Agent inventory with sponsors → limit Graph permissions → block high agent risk MT.1223 , MT.1181 , Copilot Studio checks MT.1113 – MT.1122 
 Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness SharePoint oversharing controls → sensitivity labels → then Copilot licences; Copilot Studio governance rests on Power Platform managed environments and data policies SharePoint, Purview and Copilot Studio checks 
 Insider Risk Audit on → HR connector or Defender for Endpoint onboarding, depending on the template → DLP policies at High severity for data-leak templates → Insider Risk policies MT.1172 , MT.1174 , ZTA.41045 
 Defender for Cloud Apps session control App added to Entra → CA policy with app control → session policy; blocking on endpoints needs Defender for Endpoint network protection in block mode Defender checks (none found by title for session control: a gap) 
 Third-party mail filter in front of Exchange Enhanced filtering on the inbound connector → then remove SCL -1 bypass rules ORCA.233.1 and the ORCA bypass checks 
 Defender for Identity Domain controllers onboarded to Defender for Endpoint → activate v3 sensors from the portal → health alerts MT.1059 (health issues) 
 Power Platform Managed environments → sharing limits; tenant data policies; Exchange mail-flow rules to stop flows sending mail outside Dataverse and Copilot Studio checks 
 Active Directory A large set of chains of its own: tiering → protected accounts → krbtgt rotation → delegation clean-up → LAPS → LDAP and SMB signing. Hybrid links: password hash sync, cloud Kerberos trust for Windows Hello, and Defender for Identity sensors. 270 AD checks. They cite ANSSI more than Learn, so the Windows Server mirror adds Microsoft's side. 
 Later: GitHub, Azure DevOps Each gets its own entries. CIS GitHub, Azure DevOps checks 
 Tag the change, not the test 
 Several suites check the same setting. MT.1001 , CIS.M365.5.2.2.9 , CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 and ZTA.24824 all check that CA requires a compliant device. Tag that once. 
 Many prerequisites aren't checks. "Devices are enrolled" is a state of the tenant, not a setting, so it needs a node of its own. 
 Some prerequisites have alternatives. Entra join or hybrid join will both do. 
 It's the same unit as fix once, close many (A3). One catalogue gives both. 
 So each check gets one attribute that names its change ( Step , name to settle), and a catalogue holds the changes and how they relate. That follows the framework files: the mapping lives on the test, and the catalogue holds the facts. 
 Relationship Meaning Example 
 Requires Must be done first, or the fix fails or locks users out Compliant-device CA needs compliance policies 
 Requires one of Any one of several will do Entra join or hybrid join 
 Only when Applies to some tenants only Password writeback, for synced users 
 Recommended first Works without it, but is safer after it Remediate high-risk users ( MT.1260 ) before the user-risk policy 
 Conflicts Can't both be on Security defaults ( MT.1021 ) and Conditional Access 
 Rollout How to switch it on Report-only, a pilot group, then everyone 
 // One change in the catalogue (field names to settle) 
{
 "Id": "ca-require-compliant-device",
 "Title": "Require a compliant device in Conditional Access",
 "Requires": ["intune-compliance-policies", "emergency-access-excluded"],
 "RequiresOneOf": [["entra-join", "hybrid-join"]],
 "OnlyWhen": { "sync-accounts-excluded": "hybrid" },
 "Rollout": ["report-only", "pilot", "all-users"],
 "Readiness": "share of sign-ins from compliant devices",
 "Learn": [{
 "Url": "https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance",
 "Says": "Create a compliance policy first and have at least one compliant device."
 }]
}
 // On the checks: [MaesterTest(Step = 'ca-require-compliant-device', ...)] 
 How to build it 
 An expert pass on the seven chains , because that's where a wrong order hurts users. 
 A machine-assisted pass over the rest. Its sources are the planning guides above plus the 514 Learn pages the check guides link, all fetched as Markdown. For each page, a model extracts the prerequisite statements (before, first, must, won't work without) with a link, rewords them, and proposes a change and its relationships. A maintainer approves, the same way the attribute review works. The Zero Trust Workshop's task mapping gives the pack's checks a first draft. 
 Unit tests to check that the catalogue has no cycles, every ID exists, every relationship cites a Learn page or a maintainer's note, and every change has a check or is marked prerequisite-only. 
 Expect most checks to have no prerequisite. Antivirus settings, sharing settings and most EIDSCA values stand alone. The value is concentrated where Conditional Access, devices and authentication meet. 
 What the report does with it 
 Blocked fixes leave the top of the plan and show their prerequisite instead. 
 A prerequisite gets credit for what it unlocks, so "enroll devices" ranks by the controls it enables, not by its own severity. 
 A deployment view shows one lane per chain, with each change marked Done, Ready, Blocked or Unknown. 
 Readiness comes from measured data (B1) before a change is switched on. 
 The How to fix tab gets the prerequisites and rollout steps from the catalogue. 
 The time-boxed plan follows the order, and the scenarios (A1) and this order work together: choose fixes that close open routes and are ready now. 
 Making it the strong point 
 Make it the spine of the report. The action plan becomes lanes of changes, and the overview opens with what you can do now, what's blocked, and what's blocking it. A ranked list of failures becomes one view among several. 
 Answer the question others skip: are you ready? Other tools say what's wrong. Maester also says whether the tenant is ready for the fix, and who it affects. That combines the prerequisites, the readiness checks and measured impact (B1), and no other tool reviewed here combines them. 
 Publish the catalogue as open knowledge. Every change cites Microsoft Learn and is reviewed in the open. maester.dev can show one page per chain, built from the catalogue. The community can add chains the way it adds checks. 
 Put benchmarks in order. CIS and CISA list their controls flat. Maester can turn "CIS Level 1" into a sequence the tenant can follow, starting with what it's ready for. 
 Let packs join in. A pack's checks can name the same changes, so the Zero Trust pack's device checks fall into the same lanes as Maester's. 
 Give it a name readers will recognise. "Defender's path" is the working name, as the counterpart of an attack path. 
 Work in another session Object facts, and what they change here 
 The session "Zero trust data in affected objects" (branch feat/zta-affected-object-facts , not committed yet) adds a public command, Add-MtAffectedObjectFact . Each fact has a name, a value shown as text, a tone (Risk, Warning, Good or Info), a source and the date its data was read. Facts attach to objects the run already lists. The Zero Trust pack reads its tenant export and adds facts to apps (permissions, consent, last sign-in, owners, credentials), users (roles, MFA, passwordless, last sign-in), devices (OS, join type, managed and compliant), agents (sponsors, owners) and Intune policies (assignments, last changed). 
 Part of this plan What the facts change 
 A2, most exposed identities Facts supply the weights: privileged roles, MFA not registered, dormant accounts, risky permissions. The Affected objects page with facts is the start of the object pages. A2 still needs to know why each check named an object. 
 Readiness in the defender's path Device facts (join type, managed and compliant) and user facts (MFA, passwordless) are readiness for each object, which is the drill-down behind a lane: "these 38 devices aren't managed". They can't give tenant-wide shares, because facts attach only to listed objects and come from the Zero Trust export only when it ran. Readiness checks still read Graph themselves, and should write facts too. 
 Tier C, question models Model answers become facts, with the model as the source and the tone Warning, such as "Looks like a service account". A reader's correction attaches to the same fact. 
 Unknown and dates Facts carry the date their data was read, so a readiness figure from an earlier Zero Trust export shows that date. 
 Privacy Every reader sees the facts, and redaction covers only user names the run knows. The same limit applies to classifying job titles (C1). 
 One request before the command ships, since it becomes public API: give each fact a stable key and a raw value next to its display text. Examples: user.mfaRegistered = false, signIn.daysSince = 143, device.joinType = hybrid, roles.privileged = true. Add a short shared list of keys too. Insights and readiness can then compute from facts without parsing English. It can be added later without breaking anything, but it costs less now. 
 Alignment Small runs, and runs outside the chains 
 Many runs aren't full runs. A user runs one check, one suite, or only GitHub or Azure DevOps checks that no chain covers. The rule for the report, the console and the output files is the same: scope everything to what ran, and never infer a status for a check that didn't run. 
 Run Report Console Output files 
 Full run A lane for every chain that has a check in the run. The overview opens with what's ready and what's blocked. One summary line: "2 changes ready, 1 blocked by ZTA.24542 " Steps in the JSON. Step and blocked-by columns in the CSV and Markdown. 
 One suite or product Only chains with a check in the run. A change whose checks weren't selected shows "Not checked in this run", with the command to include them. The line appears only when a chain is in scope Steps lists the changes in scope, with all their checks 
 1 to 3 checks No lanes. Each check shows "Before you fix this": its prerequisites, each with its status from this run, from an earlier run in the output folder (with its date), or Not checked. Nothing extra The same 
 Checks in no chain (GitHub, Azure DevOps, AD, most custom checks) Nothing changes. The view stays hidden, as views without data already are. Nothing No Steps 
 Checks that couldn't run (service not connected, no licence) Unknown, with the reason and the fix command. Never Not done. Counted with the checks that didn't run Status Unknown, with the reason code 
 Report · One check · MT.1001 Example data 
 Before you fix this 2 of 4 prerequisites not confirmed 
 Devices enroll in Intune automatically (passed in the full run on 2 Nov) ZTA.24546 
 A compliance policy covers every platform (failed on 2 Nov) ZTA.24542 
 Emergency access accounts are excluded (this run) MT.1005 
 Windows devices are joined (not checked) No check yet 
 Invoke-Maester -Step ca-require-compliant-device -IncludePrerequisites 
 Three statuses that must not blur: Not done (the check failed), Unknown (the check couldn't run), and Not checked (the run didn't select it). Headline numbers never count a change that wasn't checked. 
 Always give the command that fills the gap. The report already does this for checks that didn't run, and the defender's path adds -Step and -IncludePrerequisites to the selectors. 
 Build Steps from the full inventory, not just the rows that ran. That's the same way Frameworks comes from the framework files. The report then knows every check that maps to a change in scope, even ones the run didn't select. 
 Status from earlier runs needs results for each check from more than the newest earlier run. That's the same change as A4. An earlier status always shows its date, and is never mixed into this run's numbers.

Maester's strong point Do this first: implementation order 
 Attack-path tools (Exposure Management, BloodHound, EntraHound) show the route an attacker takes. None of them show the order a defender has to work in. Microsoft Learn does, page by page, and the report ignores it today. Three examples: 
 Compliant devices Learn warns that the CA policy won't work as intended without an Intune compliance policy. It says to create one first and have at least one compliant device. Learn 
 Risk policies Users must be registered for MFA, and synced users need password writeback, or the policy blocks them. Investigate and remediate existing risk before you turn it on. Learn 
 Token protection Needs Windows devices that are Entra joined, hybrid joined or registered, and Apple devices that are MDM-managed with the SSO plug-in. Start with a pilot in report-only. Learn 
 The risk today: the action plan ranks by severity, user impact and effort. In a tenant with no compliance policies it can put MT.1001 near the top, and following that advice locks users out. The guide for MT.1001 says only "Review the configuration described above."

 Chain Order of changes Checks that map to it Prerequisites Maester can't check yet 
 Require compliant devices Devices Entra or hybrid joined → enrolled in Intune → a compliance policy for each platform → emergency access excluded → CA requires a compliant device About 28: MT.1001 , MT.1014 , MT.1054 , MT.1188 , MT.1214 , MT.1228 – MT.1237 , CIS.M365.4.1 , 4.2 , 5.2.2.9 , 5.2.2.10 , CISA.MS.AAD.3.7 , 3.8 , ZTA.24541 – 24547 , ZTA.24824 Share of Windows devices joined; share of devices enrolled

# Schema of the [MaesterTest] attribute (docs/proposals/maester-3.0-test-attributes.md, section 2, and
# the Maester 3.0 design, sections 3.1 and 4).
#
# The engine reads [MaesterTest(...)] from a test file's AST and validates it against this table;
# a test file is never executed to read its metadata. The property list must match
# MaesterTestAttribute in src/Maester.Engine (a unit test compares them).
#
# Property keys:
#   Type             string | string[] | bool
#   Required         Always | BuiltIn (required for tests shipped with Maester) | No
#   NotRequiredWhen  the property is not required when another property has this value, for example
#                    @{ Severity = 'Info' }
#   AllowedValues    closed list, compared case-insensitively and stored in this spelling
#   ValuesFrom       the values are validated against an engine registry instead of a fixed list:
#                    ServiceRegistry, or Taxonomy.Products, Taxonomy.Features, Taxonomy.Areas and
#                    Taxonomy.ResourceTypes (assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1). A test shipped with Maester must
#                    use a registry value; a custom test may use any value that fits Pattern and MaxLength
#   Pattern          regular expression each value must match
#   MaxLength        maximum length of each value
#   Default          value used when the property is omitted (documentation; the engine applies it)
#   Description      one line, used by generated docs
@{
    SchemaVersion    = '1.0'

    # Segments of letters and digits (and '_' after the first segment) separated by '.' or '-',
    # starting with a letter and containing at least one digit or separator.
    IdPattern        = '^(?=.*[0-9.\-])[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*([.\-][A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$'
    IdMaxLength      = 64

    # ID prefixes that belong to tests shipped with Maester, MP. for Maester Packs, and the codes of the packs
    # that ship with Maester, whose IDs have no MP. prefix (ZTA. for the Zero Trust Assessment pack).
    ReservedPrefixes = @('MT.', 'CISA.', 'CIS.', 'EIDSCA.', 'ORCA.', 'AD-', 'AZDO.', 'MT1060.', 'ASD.', 'MP.', 'ZTA.')

    # Names reserved for future properties. Adding one later does not break existing tests.
    ReservedNames    = @('OptionalService', 'TimeoutSeconds')

    # Properties removed in Maester 3.0, with the message the reader gives for each.
    RemovedProperties = @{
        Category = '`Category` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Product` and `Feature`; the result''s `Block` is derived from them.'
        Preview  = '`Preview` was removed in Maester 3.0. Use `Lifecycle = ''Preview''`.'
    }

    # Parameter names a test cannot declare for configuration: the engine supplies them.
    ReservedParameterNames    = @('Instance')
    ReservedParameterPrefixes = @('Mt')

    # Types a test parameter may have (section 3.4).
    ParameterTypes   = @('int', 'bool', 'switch', 'string', 'string[]')

    Properties       = @{
        Id                 = @{
            Type        = 'string'
            Required    = 'Always'
            Pattern     = '^(?=.*[0-9.\-])[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*([.\-][A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$'
            MaxLength   = 64
            Description = 'Stable identifier. The file is Test.<Id>.ps1.'
        }
        Title              = @{
            Type        = 'string'
            Required    = 'Always'
            Pattern     = '^[^\r\n]+$'
            Description = 'One-line title shown in the report.'
        }
        Product            = @{
            Type        = 'string'
            Required    = 'BuiltIn'
            ValuesFrom  = 'Taxonomy.Products'
            Pattern     = '^[^\r\n]+$'
            MaxLength   = 40
            Description = 'Key of the product where the fix is made, for example entra. An alias such as Entra ID is stored as the key. Groups console progress and the run summary; written to the result as Product.'
        }
        RelatedProduct     = @{
            Type        = 'string[]'
            Required    = 'No'
            ValuesFrom  = 'Taxonomy.Products'
            Pattern     = '^[^\r\n]+$'
            MaxLength   = 40
            Description = 'Keys of other products the test also checks or depends on. Never the same key as Product.'
        }
        Feature            = @{
----

# the Maester 3.0 design, sections 3.1 and 4).
#
# The engine reads [MaesterTest(...)] from a test file's AST and validates it against this table;
# a test file is never executed to read its metadata. The property list must match
# MaesterTestAttribute in src/Maester.Engine (a unit test compares them).
#
# Property keys:
#   Type             string | string[] | bool
#   Required         Always | BuiltIn (required for tests shipped with Maester) | No
#   NotRequiredWhen  the property is not required when another property has this value, for example
#                    @{ Severity = 'Info' }
#   AllowedValues    closed list, compared case-insensitively and stored in this spelling
#   ValuesFrom       the values are validated against an engine registry instead of a fixed list:
#                    ServiceRegistry, or Taxonomy.Products, Taxonomy.Features, Taxonomy.Areas and
#                    Taxonomy.ResourceTypes (assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1). A test shipped with Maester must
#                    use a registry value; a custom test may use any value that fits Pattern and MaxLength
#   Pattern          regular expression each value must match
#   MaxLength        maximum length of each value
#   Default          value used when the property is omitted (documentation; the engine applies it)
#   Description      one line, used by generated docs
@{
    SchemaVersion    = '1.0'

    # Segments of letters and digits (and '_' after the first segment) separated by '.' or '-',
    # starting with a letter and containing at least one digit or separator.
    IdPattern        = '^(?=.*[0-9.\-])[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*([.\-][A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$'
    IdMaxLength      = 64

    # ID prefixes that belong to tests shipped with Maester, MP. for Maester Packs, and the codes of the packs
    # that ship with Maester, whose IDs have no MP. prefix (ZTA. for the Zero Trust Assessment pack).

    ReservedNames    = @('OptionalService', 'TimeoutSeconds')

function Resolve-MtNativePlan {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Decides, for every native test, whether it runs and if not why (design stages 5 and 6).

    .DESCRIPTION
    Gates apply in this order, and the first failing gate gives the reason (design section 6):
    invalid metadata; disabled by config; selection (IDs, excluded products, typed selectors, tags, opt-in
    service, Preview, long-running); platform; tenant type; cloud; service; licence; parameter binding.

    The default exclusions are decided by attribute, not by tag (test attribute design, section 4): a test
    with Lifecycle = 'Preview' or LongRunning is left out when the run excludes them by default
    (-AutoExcludedTag) and the test is not named by its exact ID, and a test whose service is opt-in, such
    as Active Directory, when that service is not connected.

    Each plan row has: Test, Disposition (Run, NotRun, Skipped or Error), ReasonCode, ReasonDetail,
    LegacySkipCode, Parameters (the bound hashtable), EffectiveParameters, TimeoutSeconds, Setting (the
    TestSettings row), InstancePatterns (for a family selected by instance ID) and ExactlyNamed.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Test,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [pscustomobject] $Selection,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [pscustomobject] $RunConfig,
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [pscustomobject] $TenantContext,
        # The include and exclude tags of the run, and which exclusions the engine added by default
        # (Preview, LongRunning, AD). The defaults are applied to native tests by attribute.
        [Parameter()] [string[]] $IncludeTag = @(),
        [Parameter()] [string[]] $ExcludeTag = @(),
        [Parameter()] [string[]] $AutoExcludedTag = @(),
        # Parameter values that win over the config (Invoke-MtTest -Parameter), by test ID.
        [Parameter()] [hashtable] $ParameterOverride = @{},
        [Parameter()] [switch] $DryRun
    )

    $environment = if ($RunConfig.PSObject.Properties['Environment']) { $RunConfig.Environment } else { $null }
    $enforce = @{ Service = $true; License = $true; TenantType = $false; Cloud = $false }
    if ($environment -and $environment.PSObject.Properties['Enforce'] -and $environment.Enforce) {
        foreach ($p in $environment.Enforce.PSObject.Properties) { if ($enforce.ContainsKey($p.Name)) { $enforce[$p.Name] = [bool]$p.Value } }
    }
    $execution = if ($RunConfig.PSObject.Properties['Execution']) { $RunConfig.Execution } else { $null }
    $registry = Get-MtServiceRegistry
    # Allow-list mode needs the rows that enable a test. Read them once, not once per test: a config copied
    # from 2.x has hundreds of rows.
    $allowListIds = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    if ($Selection.DefaultAction -eq 'Skip') {
        foreach ($ts in @($RunConfig.TestSettings)) {
            if ($ts -and $ts.Id -and $ts.PSObject.Properties['Enabled'] -and $ts.Enabled -eq $true) { $null = $allowListIds.Add([string]$ts.Id) }
        }
    }

    $selectorInUse = Test-MtSelectorInUse -Selection $Selection
    $userExcludeTag = @($ExcludeTag | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notin $AutoExcludedTag })
    # How a tag pattern matches a test: by one of its own tags, else by a Maester 2.x tag, else not at all.
    $matchTag = {
        param($tags, $pattern)
        foreach ($tag in $tags.Own) { if ($tag -like $pattern) { return 'Own' } }
        foreach ($tag in $tags.Legacy) { if ($tag -like $pattern) { return 'Legacy' } }
    }

function Add-MtAffectedObjectFact {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Adds facts about an object, such as its last sign-in or its expired secrets, to the Affected objects page.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack that knows more about an object than the checks that name
    it: when the object was last used, which permissions it holds, whether its credentials have expired. The facts
    are shown with the object on the Affected objects page of the HTML report and kept in the AffectedObjects of the
    results, the JSON output and the objects files.
    Facts only describe an object that the run already lists. They are merged into the record with the same System,
    Type and Id when the results are built, so adding facts about an object that no check names adds nothing to the
    report. Facts are collected only while Invoke-Maester collects affected objects; otherwise the call does nothing.
    Each fact has a Name, a Value and a Tone: Risk for something to fix, Warning for something to review, Good for a
    sign that the object is in order, and Info (the default) for anything else. Adding a fact with the same Name from
    the same Source again replaces the earlier one.
    The value is shown as text. Name counts rather than other people where you can: the page shows facts to everyone
    who reads the report, and -RedactUserIdentity replaces only the names of users the run knows.
    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Type ServicePrincipal -Id $sp.id -Source 'Contoso inventory' -Fact @(
        @{ Name = 'Last sign-in'; Value = '2026-06-15 (143 days ago)'; Tone = 'Risk' }
        @{ Name = 'Publisher'; Value = 'Third party (Contoso Ltd)' }
    )
    Adds two facts to an enterprise application.
    .EXAMPLE
    $records | Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Source 'Zero Trust Assessment' -AsOf $report.ExecutedAt
    Adds facts to many objects at once. Each record has Type, Id and Fact properties, and optionally System.
    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtAffectedObjectFact
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The object type, as the Affected objects page records it: User, Group, ServicePrincipal, AppRegistration
        # (keyed by its appId), Device, ConditionalAccessPolicy, AgentIdentity, AgentIdentityBlueprint, ConfigurationPolicy...
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Type,
        # The object's id, the same id the record uses (for an app registration, its appId).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Id,
        # The facts: hashtables or objects with Name, Value and an optional Tone (Risk, Warning, Good or Info).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [AllowEmptyCollection()]
        [object[]] $Fact,
        # Where the object lives: EntraID (the default), Intune, ExchangeOnline, GitHub...
        [Parameter(ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $System = 'EntraID',
        # What the facts come from, shown with them, for example 'Zero Trust Assessment'.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Source,
        # When the data behind the facts was read, when that is not now (a report written earlier).
        [Parameter()]
        [Nullable[datetime]] $AsOf
    )
    begin {
        $collecting = [bool]$__MtSession.IncludeAffectedObjects
        if (-not $collecting) {
            Write-Verbose 'Add-MtAffectedObjectFact: this run does not collect affected objects, so the facts are not kept.'
            return
        }
        if ($null -eq $__MtSession.AffectedObjectFacts) {
            $__MtSession.AffectedObjectFacts = [System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary[string, System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)

function Get-MtPreviousResult {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the result of the previous run on the same tenant, reduced to what a report needs to show changes.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Looks for TestResults-*.json files in -Folder, skipping -Exclude (the file this run writes) and any file that
    is not a Maester result or is for another tenant. Returns ExecutedAt, File (the file name) and Results, a map
    of test ID to result (Passed, Failed, Investigate, Error, Skipped, NotRun), of the newest earlier result, and
    History: the counts of up to -HistoryCount earlier runs, newest first, for the report's trend. Returns nothing
    when there is no earlier result for the tenant.
    Only Id and Result are kept, so the report shows which tests started or stopped failing without carrying a
    second copy of the findings. The comparison is the one Compare-MtTestResult makes. A result file starts with
    its counts, ExecutedAt and TenantId, so History reads only the start of each file; only the newest file is
    read in full.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # The output folder of the run.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyString()] [string] $Folder,
        # The tenant of this run. A result for another tenant is skipped; with no tenant, none is.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyString()] [string] $TenantId,
        # Files that are never the previous result, such as the JSON file this run writes.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [string[]] $Exclude = @(),
        # How many of the newest files are looked at.
----

MT.1034	Emergency access users should not be blocked.

MT.1021	Security Defaults are enabled.
MT.1012	At least one Conditional Access policy is configured to require MFA for risky sign-ins.
MT.1013	At least one Conditional Access policy is configured to require new password when user risk is high.

function Get-MtPreviousResult {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the result of the previous run on the same tenant, reduced to what a report needs to show changes.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Looks for TestResults-*.json files in -Folder, skipping -Exclude (the file this run writes) and any file that
    is not a Maester result or is for another tenant. Returns ExecutedAt, File (the file name) and Results, a map
    of test ID to result (Passed, Failed, Investigate, Error, Skipped, NotRun), of the newest earlier result, and
    History: the counts of up to -HistoryCount earlier runs, newest first, for the report's trend. Returns nothing
    when there is no earlier result for the tenant.
    Only Id and Result are kept, so the report shows which tests started or stopped failing without carrying a
    second copy of the findings. The comparison is the one Compare-MtTestResult makes. A result file starts with
    its counts, ExecutedAt and TenantId, so History reads only the start of each file; only the newest file is
    read in full.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # The output folder of the run.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyString()] [string] $Folder,
        # The tenant of this run. A result for another tenant is skipped; with no tenant, none is.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyString()] [string] $TenantId,
        # Files that are never the previous result, such as the JSON file this run writes.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [string[]] $Exclude = @(),
        # How many of the newest files are looked at.

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reads the tenant context in steps, and says after each step what it found.
    .DESCRIPTION
    The work of Get-MtTenantContext. Some of the facts need a request to a service (the organization, the
    licences, and for some services whether the token still works), so reading all of them takes a second
    or more. -OnStep is called as each part is known, so that a caller with a display can show the account
    first and fill in the rest as it arrives:
      Account       TenantId, Account, AuthType, Graph    from the Graph session, without a request
      Organization  TenantName, PrimaryDomain             after the organization was read
      Service       Name, Connected                       once for each service that was checked
    A step that throws is ignored: the display must not cost the run its tenant context.
    .PARAMETER Service
    The services to check the connection of. Defaults to every service in the service registry.
    .PARAMETER Environment
    The Environment section of a Maester config, whose values replace detected ones.
    .PARAMETER OnStep
    Called with the name of the step and a hashtable of what it found.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Service,
        [Parameter()]
        [AllowNull()]
        [object] $Environment,
